Notebooks: 'Jupyter Notebooks in VS Code' (https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/jupyter-notebooks, fetched) covers Variable Explorer, Data Viewer and export to .py, but does not describe Copilot in notebooks. Data Wrangler quick start: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/data-wrangler-quick-start (link only).

resources.title: Securing AI-assisted development in VS Code (prompt injection, Workspace Trust, approvals, sandboxing)
resources.summary: Explains the risks of agents and MCP servers, with prompt injection through tool output as the central concern. It recommends Restricted Mode (Workspace Trust) for untrusted projects and reviewing edits, terminal commands and tool calls through approval prompts.
resources.wiki_use: Pair it with the Claude Code security page so students see the same principles across tools.
resources.notes: Related: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/approvals and https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/agent-sandboxing (links only).

resources.title: Codex documentation: CLI, IDE extension, cloud, and app (ChatGPT Learn)
resources.summary: Codex is OpenAI's coding agent. It runs in the ChatGPT desktop, web and mobile apps, as the Codex CLI (works on local files, scriptable with `codex exec`), as an IDE extension (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf; JetBrains and Xcode integrations), and as Codex Cloud (remote tasks that end in a PR). It is included in every ChatGPT plan, Free through Enterprise.
resources.wiki_use: Alternative agent for students who already pay for ChatGPT Plus. The Free plan gives limited Codex access for quick tasks.
resources.notes: developers.openai.com/codex now 302-redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs. Pricing (https://learn.chatgpt.com/codex/pricing, fetched 2026-10-23): Free $0 (limited); Go $8/month; Plus $20; Pro from $100 ($100/$200/$500); Business $20/user/month annual or $25 monthly; Edu and Enterprise by quote. CLI: https://learn.chatgpt.com/codex/cli; IDE: https://learn.chatgpt.com/codex/ide; Cloud: https://learn.chatgpt.com/codex/cloud. The CLI is open source (Apache-2.0) at https://github.com/openai/codex.

resources.title: Codex sandboxing and approval modes
resources.summary: Explains Codex's OS-enforced sandbox modes (read-only, workspace-write as the local default, and full access) and the approval policies that decide when the agent must stop and ask.
resources.wiki_use: Comparison row on the 'running agents safely' page: Codex's workspace-write mode next to Claude Code's sandbox and VS Code approvals.
resources.notes: Related: https://learn.chatgpt.com/codex/agent-approvals-security and https://learn.chatgpt.com/codex/security (links from the docs hub).

resources.section: AI inside notebooks and data apps
resources.title: Data analysis with ChatGPT
resources.summary: ChatGPT analyzes uploaded spreadsheets (.xls, .xlsx, .csv), PDFs and text or data files (JSON, XML, YAML) in a Python environment with no internet access. Availability and limits depend on model, plan and workspace settings.
resources.wiki_use: Parallel to the Claude file-creation lab: students run the same RFM or segmentation prompt in both tools and compare the code and numbers each produces.
resources.notes: The article does not list plans per feature. It warns that large or complex files may not be fully analyzed, which is a good prompt to teach 'check the row count'.

resources.title: ChatGPT Edu (ChatGPT for education)
resources.summary: A campus-licensed ChatGPT workspace with the flagship model, data analysis, custom GPTs, an admin console and SSO. OpenAI states that Edu data and conversations are not used for training. It is sold to institutions through sales, with no individual student offer on the page.
resources.wiki_use: Explain to students why institutional licenses differ from personal accounts. At UIUC the related 'Illinois ChatGPT' license is for faculty and staff only.
resources.notes: Launch post (May 30, 2024): https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-edu/. The page does not say whether Edu includes Codex, but the Codex pricing page lists Edu among the plans that include it. chatgpt.com/students could not be fetched (client error), so I could not verify any current consumer student offer.

resources.title: Prompt engineering (OpenAI API docs)
resources.summary: OpenAI's guide to consistent results: choosing between reasoning and GPT models, instructions and message roles, Markdown or XML structure, few-shot examples, RAG context, prompt caching, and model-specific advice for coding and agentic tasks.
resources.wiki_use: Second canonical prompting reference next to Anthropic's. Students compare the two and distill a one-page 'prompting for analysis code' checklist.
resources.notes: platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-engineering 302-redirects here. A Codex-specific prompting page appears in the navigation at https://developers.openai.com/codex/prompting (not opened).

resources.title: Enterprise privacy at OpenAI (business data commitments)
resources.summary: By default OpenAI does not train on business data from ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Edu or the API. Admins set retention for Enterprise and Edu, and API data is generally kept up to 30 days. Personal (consumer) accounts are handled differently and may be used for training.
resources.wiki_use: Data-privacy page: the core lesson that the same model under a different account type carries different data terms. Never paste client or customer PII into a personal account.

resources.title: Gemini CLI (google-gemini/gemini-cli) and docs
resources.summary: An open-source terminal agent for Gemini models, with GEMINI.md context files, MCP servers, extensions, sandboxing and trusted folders. The README still advertises a free tier (60 requests/minute and 1,000/day with a personal Google account), but see the notes.
resources.wiki_use: Mention it as historical context only. Point students to Antigravity CLI or another tool instead (see gemini-cli-to-antigravity-transition).
resources.notes: IMPORTANT: The docs (https://geminicli.com/docs/) say 'Unpaid tier and Google One users: Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on June 18th, 2026.' The README's free-tier description looks out of date. Gemini CLI is still available through paid API keys and Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licenses. Free course: DeepLearning.AI 'Gemini CLI: Code & Create with an Open-Source Agent' (Jack Wotherspoon, Google; 1h23m, beginner; https://www.deeplearning.ai/short-courses/gemini-cli-code-and-create-with-an-open-source-agent/, fetched). It includes a data-analysis dashboard lesson that mixes local CSVs with cloud data, and the page now lists a 'Gemini CLI Deprecation for Free, Pro, and Ultra Users' reading.

resources.title: An important update: Transitioning Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI
resources.summary: Google announced on May 19, 2026 that on June 18, 2026 Gemini CLI and the Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions would stop serving Google AI Pro/Ultra subscribers and free individual users. Antigravity CLI, a new Go-based terminal agent that shares a harness with the Antigravity 2.0 desktop app, replaces them. Enterprise Code Assist customers keep Gemini CLI.
resources.wiki_use: Use it as a dated warning on the tools page, and as an M8 example of how fast the AI tooling market shifts (tutorials from 2025 will mislead students).
resources.notes: Antigravity CLI supports Agent Skills, hooks, subagents and plugins (formerly extensions), but did not launch with full Gemini CLI feature parity. The post does not state a free-tier limit.

resources.title: Google Antigravity (agentic IDE, desktop app, CLI, SDK)
resources.summary: Google's agent-first development platform: Antigravity IDE (an agentic IDE with an agent manager and artifacts), the Antigravity App for coordinating multiple agents, a CLI (`agy`), extensions for VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio, Zed and Xcode, and a Python SDK. It supports SKILL.md skills, rules and MCP, with tool approval gates, a terminal sandbox and sandboxed browser automation.
resources.wiki_use: Google's replacement for the free Gemini CLI path. The free individual tier makes it viable for students who have no paid subscription.
resources.notes: It exists (verified). Pricing (https://antigravity.google/pricing): Free individual tier ($0, a range of agent models, unlimited Tab completions, basic weekly rate limits); Google AI Pro and Ultra add higher limits and AI credits; business plans through Google Cloud. Docs: https://antigravity.google/docs/overview. Security: https://antigravity.google/docs/permissions/ and https://antigravity.google/docs/sandbox/. The docs page did not mention AGENTS.md. Desktop builds for macOS, Windows and Linux.

resources.title: Jules: Google's asynchronous coding agent
resources.summary: An autonomous agent that clones a GitHub repo into a cloud VM, proposes a plan, and opens a PR for bug fixes, tests, version bumps or features. Plans: free (15 tasks/day, 3 concurrent), AI Pro (100/day), AI Ultra (300/day).
resources.wiki_use: Optional comparison with Copilot's cloud agent and Codex Cloud: assign the same 'write unit tests for clv.py' issue to each and compare the PRs.
resources.notes: The fetched page listed Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro as the models, which may be out of date. App: https://jules.google.com/.

resources.section: AI inside notebooks and data apps
resources.title: Google Colab: AI-powered notebooks (Gemini in Colab)
resources.summary: Colab's landing page presents it as an AI coding assistant. Gemini generates, explains, debugs, refactors and documents code from plain-language prompts, and 'autonomous analysis' generates and runs code to answer questions about data. Pro and Pro+ add compute and background execution.
resources.wiki_use: Default environment for in-class labs. The wiki can link 'Open in Colab' badges for every notebook, with Gemini as the built-in assistant.
resources.notes: colab.google now 302-redirects here. Try AI-first Colab at https://colab.new/ (link only). Teaching posts: https://medium.com/google-colab/tagged/education (link only). Colab AI features require age 18+ and may vary by locale (see colab-faq-ai-privacy).

resources.title: Colab FAQ: AI features, data use, and Colab Pro for Education
resources.summary: Colab's AI features are on by default for eligible users aged 18+. Google collects prompts, related code, outputs and feedback, human reviewers may read them, and data is kept up to 18 months. Users are asked not to include sensitive or personally identifying information. Colab Pro for Education (free Pro for US students) is no longer open to new signups.
resources.wiki_use: Key slide for the privacy lesson: in Colab, never paste customer PII into a Gemini prompt, and use synthetic or anonymized course datasets.
resources.notes: By default Colab AI cannot read Drive files or secrets, but it can write code that does when you ask. Note the contrast with Google Workspace for Education terms on the UIUC page.

resources.section: AI inside notebooks and data apps
resources.title: Data Science Agent in Colab: The future of data analysis with Gemini
resources.authors: Fine, J.; Kolla, M.; Soloducho, I. (Google)
resources.summary: Announces Colab's Data Science Agent. You upload a data file and describe a goal in the Gemini side panel, and the agent generates a complete, executable notebook (imports, loading, cleaning, plots). The post warns that the agent may make mistakes and cites a 4th-place finish on the DABStep data-agent benchmark.
resources.wiki_use: Demo in M2 or M3: students let the agent build a first-pass EDA or regression notebook, then audit every cell for correctness.
resources.notes: Published March 3, 2025. At launch it was for users 18+ in select countries. On the current Colab page this capability appears as 'autonomous analysis'. Benchmark: https://huggingface.co/spaces/adyen/DABstep (link only).

resources.title: Google AI Pro for students (free for 1 year)
resources.summary: As of 2026-10-23: eligible US college students aged 18+ get Google AI Pro free for one year (higher Gemini limits, 5 TB storage and other features) if they redeem by December 31, 2026. Eligibility is verified each year. A payment method is required, and the plan auto-renews at $19.99/month unless cancelled.
resources.wiki_use: Day-one setup: remind students to set a calendar reminder to cancel before the renewal charge. AI Pro also raises Antigravity and Jules limits.
resources.notes: The page does not mention NotebookLM, Jules or Colab. Students whose 2025 AI Pro trial expired can re-qualify.

resources.section: AI inside notebooks and data apps
resources.title: Jupyter AI (jupyterlab/jupyter-ai) v3
resources.summary: An open-source JupyterLab extension that connects AI agents (Claude, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Goose, Kiro, Mistral Vibe, OpenCode and others) to notebooks through the Agent Client Protocol. A built-in Jupyter MCP server lets agents edit and run cells, and a permission system asks before any write or command.
resources.wiki_use: For students on local JupyterLab: shows agents working inside the notebook with approval prompts, in contrast with copy-pasting into chat.
resources.notes: Docs: https://jupyter-ai.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ (v3.2.0). The older v2 docs, with %%ai magics and provider-based chat, are at https://jupyter-ai.readthedocs.io/en/v2/.

resources.section: AI inside notebooks and data apps
resources.title: marimo: generate notebooks with AI (built-in assistant, marimo pair, text-to-notebook)
resources.summary: Three AI routes in the reactive marimo notebook: (1) 'marimo pair', which lets agent CLIs such as Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode read variables and run or edit cells in a live notebook; (2) the editor's assistant (chat in Manual, Ask, Agent and Code modes; cell generation; inline completion; providers OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Copilot, Bedrock, Ollama); and (3) `marimo new PROMPT` to generate a whole notebook.
resources.wiki_use: Recommended for the notebook-vs-script lesson. marimo notebooks are plain .py files, which diff cleanly in Git and are easy for agents to edit.
resources.notes: Editor assistant: https://docs.marimo.io/guides/editor_features/ai_completion/ (fetched). marimo pair: https://docs.marimo.io/guides/generate_with_ai/marimo_pair/ (link). The agents panel is experimental.

resources.section: AI inside notebooks and data apps
resources.title: Posit Assistant in Positron (replaces Positron Assistant and Databot)
resources.summary: Positron, Posit's data-science IDE, ships Posit Assistant as its default AI experience from Positron 2026.07, replacing Positron Assistant and Databot. It uses session context (loaded data, plots, console history, variable types) for EDA, cleaning, modeling and app building in R and Python, and includes skills such as shiny-bslib, quarto-authoring and predictive-modeling-r.
resources.wiki_use: Best fit for students using R alongside Python. Demo how session-aware context (it 'sees' the data frame) changes the quality of AI-generated analysis code.
resources.notes: Positron Assistant and Databot are marked deprecated (Databot page: https://positron.posit.co/databot.html). Bring-your-own-key: Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, GitHub Copilot or OpenAI, or Posit AI Pass (whether AI Pass costs money was not stated). No student offer. Docs: https://assistant.posit.co/docs/getting-started/. Provider privacy: https://positron.posit.co/assistant-provider-info.html.

resources.title: Windsurf, now Devin Desktop (Cognition)
resources.summary: Windsurf, the agentic IDE, has been renamed Devin Desktop. It keeps the Windsurf IDE and adds an Agent Command Center for local and cloud agents. Plans: Free $0, Pro $20/month, Max $200, Teams $80/month plus $40 per seat, Enterprise.
resources.wiki_use: Use it in M8 as a case on AI-tooling industry dynamics. The 2025 acquisition saga is a good IO discussion of acqui-hires and licensing.
resources.notes: windsurf.com/editor 302-redirects here. ACQUISITION HISTORY: OpenAI's roughly $3B deal for Windsurf collapsed on July 11, 2025, and Google DeepMind hired CEO Varun Mohan, co-founder Douglas Chen and researchers under a nonexclusive technology license reported by Bloomberg at about $2.4B (TechCrunch, Maxwell Zeff, July 11, 2025: https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/11/windsurfs-ceo-goes-to-google-openais-acquisition-falls-apart/). Cognition then signed a definitive agreement to acquire Windsurf's IP, product, brand and employees (Cognition blog, July 14, 2025: https://cognition.com/blog/windsurf, redirected from cognition.ai). The Windsurf JetBrains plugin is still available.

resources.title: Build Apps with Windsurf's AI Coding Agents (DeepLearning.AI)
resources.summary: A 1h30m beginner course on agentic IDE workflows: multi-file edits, debugging and auto-fixing tests, how agents use tools and context, upgrading legacy code, and building a Wikipedia data-analysis app with caching and visualization.
resources.wiki_use: Optional. Its agent concepts transfer to any IDE, though the product is now Devin Desktop.
resources.notes: Year approximate (2025). Free access 'for a limited time during the platform beta'. Graded items need Pro.

resources.section: AI inside notebooks and data apps
resources.title: Replit Agent
resources.summary: A browser-based AI builder that turns plain-language descriptions into deployed apps, data visualizations and slides. It plans, writes code, sets up infrastructure and tests, with a Plan mode for reviewing the task list first. Free Mode covers everyday use, and paid Power and Max modes handle harder work.
resources.wiki_use: For teams that want an interactive dashboard to accompany their blog post without managing hosting.
resources.notes: Pricing (https://replit.com/pricing, 2026-10-23): Core $20/month ($18 annual), Pro $100 ($90), Enterprise custom. Free or Starter details were not stated clearly on the pricing page. No education offer listed.

resources.section: AI inside notebooks and data apps
resources.title: Lovable (AI full-stack web app builder)
resources.summary: Builds and deploys web apps (frontend, backend, database, auth) from natural-language prompts, with editable code synced to GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket. Pricing is credit-based.
resources.wiki_use: Option for teams building an interactive companion app, such as a CLV calculator, for their project.
resources.notes: Student discount (https://lovable.dev/students): 50% off Pro for up to 12 months ($12.50 instead of $25/month, 100 credits/month), verified with a school email and no card required. The pricing page did not show free-plan limits when fetched.

resources.section: AI inside notebooks and data apps
resources.title: v0 by Vercel
resources.summary: An AI agent that builds landing pages, dashboards and full-stack apps (Next.js, Tailwind, shadcn/ui) from prompts or mockups, with one-click deploy to Vercel and GitHub sync.
resources.wiki_use: For students who want a polished front-end dashboard for project results.
resources.notes: Pricing (https://v0.app/pricing, 2026-10-23): Free (7 messages/day, deploy, GitHub sync); Plus $30/user/month; Business $100/user/month (training opt-out by default); Enterprise custom. Note that the free and Plus tiers do not opt out of training by default. A similar builder: Bolt.new by StackBlitz (https://bolt.new, fetched) builds websites and apps from chat, with Bolt Cloud hosting, databases and auth. Its landing page says 'start for free' but lists no limits or prices.

resources.section: AI inside notebooks and data apps
resources.title: Julius AI
resources.summary: A chat-first AI workspace for analyzing uploaded data and producing charts, dashboards, presentations and reports, with connectors to Google Drive, OneDrive and SharePoint.
resources.wiki_use: Use it as a contrast case: compare a no-code AI analysis app's output with code-first analysis (Colab plus agent), with emphasis on transparency and reproducibility.
resources.notes: Pricing (https://julius.ai/pricing, 2026-10-23): Free (daily credits, 'Julius Lite' models); Plus $20/month ($16 annual, 2,000 credits); Pro $45 ($37); Business $450 ($375); Enterprise custom. No student discount listed. The pricing page does not say whether user data trains models (it cites SOC 2 Type II). A similar tool: Deepnote's Education plan (https://deepnote.com/education, fetched) is free with a school email but excludes Deepnote AI.

resources.title: Agent Skills with Anthropic (DeepLearning.AI)
resources.summary: A 2h19m beginner course: skill folder structure and SKILL.md, progressive disclosure, how skills compare with tools, MCP and subagents, pre-built skills (Excel, PowerPoint, skill creation), custom skills, and using skills across Claude.ai, Claude Code, the API and the Agent SDK.
resources.wiki_use: Assign it before students write a team analysis skill.
resources.notes: The page does not state a price; quizzes and certificates need DeepLearning.AI Pro. Year inferred (late 2025 or 2026), not confirmed on the page.

resources.title: Generative AI for Beginners (21 lessons)
resources.summary: A free 21-lesson course with Python and TypeScript samples on LLM fundamentals, prompt engineering, text generation, chat, RAG, function calling (lesson 11) and AI agents (lesson 17). The repo has about 122k stars.
resources.wiki_use: Background for M5 and M7. Embed or adapt the prompt-engineering and function-calling lessons as optional readings.
resources.notes: The repo is large (translations and images), so clone with --depth 1 or a sparse checkout of the needed lesson folders rather than mirroring everything. It does not cover AI coding tools or MCP; Microsoft has a separate 'MCP for Beginners' course, which I did not verify. Many samples assume Azure OpenAI or GitHub Models.

resources.title: My LLM codegen workflow atm
resources.summary: A widely cited workflow: brainstorm a spec with an LLM asking one question at a time (spec.md), have a reasoning model write a step-by-step plan and prompts (prompt_plan.md, todo.md), then execute step by step with tests. Brownfield work uses repomix to pack context for review and for finding missing tests.
resources.wiki_use: Assigned reading. Students apply the spec, plan, execute loop to their team project and commit spec.md and todo.md to the repo.
resources.notes: Published February 16, 2025. Follow-up 'Basic Claude Code' (May 8, 2025): https://harper.blog/2025/05/08/basic-claude-code/ (link from the post).

resources.title: Using Git with coding agents
resources.summary: Git as the safety net for agent work. Have agents init repos, commit and review recent commits to load context; explain merge, rebase and squash; resolve conflicts with tests; recover lost work from the reflog; write git-bisect test scripts; and tidy history.
resources.wiki_use: Short reading for the GitHub-workflow lab: commit before every agent run, and review the diff before accepting.
resources.notes: Last updated March 21, 2026 (from page metadata).

resources.title: What to look for in a code review (Google Engineering Practices)
resources.summary: Google's reviewer checklist: design, functionality and edge cases, complexity and over-engineering, tests that actually fail when code breaks, naming, and comments that explain why.
resources.wiki_use: Adapt it into the course's 'AI-generated analysis code review checklist', adding data-specific items: row counts, joins, missing values, units, and reproducing headline numbers.
resources.notes: The page does not state a license; it says the site is open source on GitHub. The year is approximate (the guide was first published around 2019) and was not verified.

resources.title: pandera: statistical data testing for DataFrames
resources.summary: A lightweight library for declaring DataFrame schemas (types, ranges, allowed values) and validating pandas or polars data with `schema.validate()`. Failures surface silent errors that AI-written cleaning code can introduce.
resources.wiki_use: Exercise: students ask the agent to write the cleaning step and also a pandera schema plus pytest assertions, then deliberately break the data to check that the tests catch it.
resources.notes: Docs: https://pandera.readthedocs.io. In recent versions use `import pandera.pandas as pa`; the top-level import is deprecated. Pair with pytest: https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/getting-started.html (fetched).

resources.title: The Turing Way: Guide for Reproducible Research
resources.summary: An open handbook by more than 300 contributors. Its chapters on version control, testing, reproducible environments and code review give a vendor-neutral base for checking any analysis, including AI-written code.
resources.wiki_use: Link the Testing (https://book.the-turing-way.org/reproducible-research/testing) and Reproducible Environments (https://book.the-turing-way.org/reproducible-research/renv) chapters from the project-requirements page.
resources.notes: Subchapter URLs come from the fetched page. CC BY lets the wiki adapt excerpts with attribution.

resources.title: Good enough practices in scientific computing
resources.authors: Wilson, G.; Bryan, J.; Cranston, K.; Kitzes, J.; Nederbragt, L.; Teal, T. K.
resources.summary: A minimal set of practices for newcomers: keep raw data unchanged, script every processing step, write short well-named functions, state dependencies explicitly, use a consistent project layout with README, LICENSE and CITATION files, and use version control.
resources.wiki_use: Academic anchor for the team-project repo rubric. Students can have the agent scaffold this layout.

resources.title: uv: Python package and project manager
resources.summary: A fast Rust-based replacement for pip, virtualenv, pip-tools and pyenv. It provides a universal lockfile (`uv lock`, `uv sync`), `uv run` for isolated execution, and inline script dependency metadata (`uv add --script`).
resources.wiki_use: Require a uv lockfile (or requirements.txt for Colab) in team repos, so the analysis an agent produced on one laptop reruns on the grader's machine.
resources.notes: Repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv. I did not verify the license from the fetched page. In Colab, students can instead pin versions in a requirements.txt and run `pip install -r`.

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
resources.summary: The standard list of LLM application risks: LLM01 prompt injection, LLM02 sensitive information disclosure, LLM03 supply chain, LLM04 data and model poisoning, LLM05 improper output handling, LLM06 excessive agency, LLM07 system prompt leakage, LLM08 vector and embedding weaknesses, LLM09 misinformation, LLM10 unbounded consumption.
resources.wiki_use: Security page backbone. Map LLM01, LLM02, LLM06 and LLM09 to concrete student behaviors with agents and data.
resources.notes: Agent-specific companion: 'OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026' (published December 9, 2025; https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/, fetched). Its landing page does not list the ten items; the PDF is at https://genai.owasp.org/download/52117/?tmstv=1765059207 (not opened).

resources.title: The lethal trifecta for AI agents: private data, untrusted content, and external communication
resources.summary: An agent that combines access to private data, exposure to untrusted content and the ability to communicate externally can be steered by prompt injection into leaking data. Guardrails help only partly, so avoid giving one agent all three.
resources.wiki_use: The single most teachable security concept. Students check their own setup (for example customer CSV + web browsing + MCP email = all three) against it.

resources.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
resources.authors: Greshake, K.; Abdelnabi, S.; Mishra, S.; Endres, C.; Holz, T.; Fritz, M.
resources.summary: The foundational paper on indirect prompt injection. Instructions hidden in content an LLM retrieves can hijack the application, causing data theft, worming and contamination of information ecosystems. Demonstrated against Bing Chat and code-completion engines.
resources.wiki_use: Academic citation for the security page, and for M5's point that scraped social-media text may itself contain injected instructions.
resources.notes: The arXiv page lists no venue. The paper is widely cited as appearing at ACM AISec 2023, which I did not verify here.

resources.title: Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?
resources.authors: Perry, N.; Srivastava, M.; Kumar, D.; Boneh, D.
resources.summary: In a user study, participants with an AI assistant wrote significantly less secure code yet were more confident it was secure. Participants who trusted the AI less and refined their prompts more produced fewer vulnerabilities.
resources.wiki_use: Evidence for the course norm 'confidence is not correctness'. Pair it with an in-class exercise auditing AI-generated code.
resources.notes: The arXiv page shows the ACM DOI but not the venue name. CCS 2023 is inferred from the DOI and should be confirmed before citing.

resources.title: Online Retail II
resources.summary: 1,067,371 invoice lines from a UK online retailer, Dec 2009 to Dec 2011, in a single 43.5 MB xlsx file (invoice, stock code, quantity, price, customer ID, country).
resources.wiki_use: Default dataset for M2 cleaning and visualization and for M4 RFM segmentation and CLV exercises. It is small enough for Colab.
resources.notes: The original Online Retail (I) has 541,909 rows (Dec 2010 to Dec 2011), 22.6 MB, CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.24432/C5BW33, at https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/352/online+retail . Expect cancellations/returns and missing customer IDs to clean; check these on load.

resources.title: Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist
resources.summary: About 100,000 orders from the Brazilian marketplace Olist, in relational tables covering customers, sellers, products, payments, delivery and review scores/text. About 126 MB.
resources.wiki_use: Strong team-project dataset: practice joins, analyze delivery delay against review score, use the Portuguese review text in M5 (a good LLM-translation exercise), and model repeat purchase in M7.
resources.notes: The license, size and 'last updated 2021-10-01' come from the Kaggle API. The companion 'Marketing Funnel by Olist' dataset (Kaggle ref olistbr/marketing-funnel-olist) has about 8k marketing-qualified leads from Jun 2017 to Jun 2018, 875 KB, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and joins to orders via seller_id.

resources.title: dunnhumby Source Files: The Complete Journey, Breakfast at the Frat, Carbo-Loading, Let's Get Sort-of-Real
resources.summary: Free retail datasets. The Complete Journey has two years of all-category transactions for 2,500 frequent-shopper households, with demographics and direct-marketing campaign history. Breakfast at the Frat has 156 weeks of store-week sales, prices and promotions for four categories. Carbo-Loading has household transactions in pasta, sauce, syrup and pancake mix. Let's Get Sort-of-Real is a large simulated set (4.3 GB full, with smaller samples).
resources.wiki_use: Use The Complete Journey for campaign-response and CLV projects, and Breakfast at the Frat for M3 price/promotion regression and elasticity exercises.
resources.notes: Direct downloads, with no registration requirement visible. The license is on a linked Terms and Conditions page that was not reviewed. A Kaggle mirror of The Complete Journey (ref frtgnn/dunnhumby-the-complete-journey, 847 MB, listed under ODbL) also exists. Separately, 84.51 released a different 'Complete Journey' (801 households, one year, about 1.47M transactions) as the pip-installable completejourney_py (MIT code, Parquet): https://github.com/cunningjames/completejourney_py . Its README describes that data as simulated and for educational use only, which makes it the easiest Colab option. Not confirmed whether downloads require a sign-up; the page's download buttons are script-driven.

resources.title: The Instacart Online Grocery Shopping Dataset 2017
resources.license: Provided as-is for non-commercial use, subject to Instacart Terms (per release post)
resources.summary: Over 3 million grocery orders from more than 200,000 users, with 4 to 100 orders each, including order sequence, timing and product/aisle/department.
resources.wiki_use: Use for market-basket (association-rule) analysis, reorder prediction and product-embedding exercises.
resources.notes: The post links to https://www.instacart.com/datasets/grocery-shopping-2017 for download (not tested; the original S3 hosting may be gone). A Kaggle mirror (ref psparks/instacart-market-basket-analysis, 713 MB) is labeled CC0 by its uploader. That conflicts with Instacart's non-commercial terms, so follow Instacart's terms.

resources.title: H&M Personalized Fashion Recommendations (Kaggle competition data)
resources.summary: Kaggle competition data for building product recommendations from customers' previous purchases.
resources.wiki_use: Optional advanced team-project dataset for recommender systems. Give students a pre-sampled slice.
resources.notes: Only the competition metadata could be fetched; the Data and Rules tabs did not load. The data is known to include article metadata, customers, transactions and product images and to run to many GB, but file sizes and the license were not verified. Students must accept the competition rules to download.

resources.title: Google Analytics 4 sample ecommerce dataset (Google Merchandise Store) in BigQuery
resources.license: Docs CC BY 4.0; code samples Apache 2.0; dataset under Google terms
resources.summary: Obfuscated GA4 event export from the Google Merchandise Store, covering Nov 1, 2020 to Jan 31, 2021. Query it as bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*; it runs within the BigQuery Sandbox or free tier.
resources.wiki_use: Web-analytics lab: SQL from Colab for funnels, sessions, traffic sources and purchase conversion. It is a natural place for AI-assisted SQL writing, with students checking the generated queries against the schema.
resources.notes: Contains placeholder values (<Other>, NULL, empty strings) and has limited internal consistency. The older Universal Analytics sample (bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*, session-level, obfuscated GA360 data around Aug 2016 to Aug 2017) is documented at https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/7586738 .

resources.title: Telco Customer Churn (IBM sample data)
resources.summary: IBM's sample telecom customer table with demographics, services, charges and a churn flag. It is the standard churn-classification teaching dataset (about 1 MB CSV).
resources.wiki_use: Use for logistic regression and tree-based churn models in M3/M7, plus retention targeting and the link to CLV.
resources.notes: Also on Kaggle (ref blastchar/telco-customer-churn, 977,501 bytes, license listed as 'Data files (c) Original Authors'). IBM Cognos docs describe an extended five-file version with CLTV and churn-score fields: https://www.ibm.com/docs/SSEP7J_11.1.0/com.ibm.swg.ba.cognos.ig_smples.doc/c_telco_dm_sam.html

resources.title: Bank Marketing
resources.authors: Moro, S.; Rita, P.; Cortez, P.
resources.summary: 45,211 records from a Portuguese bank's phone-based direct-marketing campaigns, with client attributes, contact history and whether the client subscribed to a term deposit. Under 1 MB zipped.
resources.wiki_use: Response-model exercise: logistic regression against gradient boosting, lift/gain charts and campaign targeting.
resources.notes: Associated paper: Moro, Cortez & Rita (2014), 'A data-driven approach to predict the success of bank telemarketing', Decision Support Systems. The year shown is the paper's. Call duration is a common leakage teaching point; confirm in the UCI variable notes.

resources.title: Online Shoppers Purchasing Intention Dataset
resources.summary: 12,330 e-commerce sessions with 17 session-level clickstream features and a purchase label (1 MB CSV).
resources.wiki_use: Quick in-class classification lab with class imbalance; it complements GA4 with a tidy, flat table.
resources.notes: Paper: Sakar, Polat, Katircioglu & Kastro (2019), Neural Computing & Applications. The year shown is the paper's.

resources.title: Kevin Hillstrom MineThatData E-Mail Analytics Challenge dataset
resources.summary: 64,000 recent customers randomly split into a Men's e-mail, a Women's e-mail or no e-mail, with two-week visit, conversion and spend outcomes (about 5 MB CSV).
resources.wiki_use: Flagship M6 experiment dataset: estimate effects by arm, explore heterogeneous effects and build uplift targeting policies. sklift.datasets.fetch_hillstrom() loads it in one line.
resources.notes: The original 2008 post is on blog.minethatdata.com; a direct file URL was not verified. scikit-uplift also has loaders for the Criteo, X5 RetailHero, Lenta and MegaFon uplift datasets: https://www.uplift-modeling.com/en/latest/api/datasets/index.html

resources.title: Criteo Uplift Prediction Dataset (v2.1)
resources.authors: Diemert, E.; Betlei, A.; Renaudin, C.; Amini, M.-R.
resources.venue: Criteo AI Lab; AdKDD & TargetAd Workshop at KDD 2018
resources.summary: 13,979,592 users from randomized ad incrementality tests (v2.1, 297 MB compressed). It has 12 anonymized features, a treatment flag, an exposure flag and visit/conversion labels; the treatment ratio is 0.85.
resources.wiki_use: Advanced uplift exercise, plus a lesson on noncompliance (assigned treatment vs actual exposure). Subsample it for Colab.
resources.notes: Use v2.1. The original 25.3M-row release had a leak that inflated uplift. oa_url is the benchmark paper PDF (seen in search).

resources.title: Criteo Attribution Modeling for Bidding Dataset
resources.authors: Diemert, E.; Meynet, J.; Lefortier, D.; Galland, P.
resources.venue: Criteo AI Lab; AdKDD & TargetAd Workshop at KDD 2017
resources.summary: A 30-day sample of Criteo traffic: 16.5M impressions, 45K conversions and 700 campaigns, with clicks, conversions, attribution flags and cost (623 MB compressed). Ships with a reproduction notebook.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor demo for M6/M8 on last-click vs model-based attribution. Too large for routine student download.

resources.title: Open Bandit Dataset and Open Bandit Pipeline
resources.license: Code Apache 2.0; data license not stated (full data for research use)
resources.summary: Logged recommendation data from a 7-day experiment on the ZOZOTOWN fashion e-commerce site, where uniform-random and Bernoulli Thompson Sampling policies served items. Comes with the obp Python library for off-policy evaluation.
resources.wiki_use: M8 demo on bandits and on evaluating a new recommendation policy from logged data. A small sample ships in the repo.
resources.notes: The README says the small version is in obd/; the folder listing itself was blocked. The full data is at research.zozo.com.

resources.title: The Upworthy Research Archive
resources.authors: Matias, J. N.; Munger, K.; Aubin Le Quere, M.; Ebersole, C.
resources.summary: Headline A/B tests Upworthy ran from Jan 2013 to Apr 2015: 32,487 experiments in total, including a 4,873-experiment exploratory set released for analysis and teaching.
resources.wiki_use: Real field experiments for M6 (multiple arms, effect sizes, multiple testing) and M5 (which headline text features drive clicks, including LLM-coded features).
resources.notes: Download from OSF at https://osf.io/jd64p/ . The site links a June 2024 update on the reliability of platform A/B-test archives; read it before analysis.

resources.title: Amazon Reviews 2023 (Amazon Reviews'23)
resources.authors: Hou, Y.; Li, J.; He, Z.; Yan, A.; Chen, X.; McAuley, J.
resources.venue: McAuley Lab, UC San Diego; arXiv:2403.03952
resources.summary: 571.54M reviews from 54.51M users on 48.19M items in 33 categories (May 1996 to Sep 2023). Includes ratings, text, helpful votes, images, item metadata (price, descriptions) and bought-together links.
resources.wiki_use: Have students pick a small category (Subscription_Boxes about 16K ratings, Magazine_Subscriptions about 71K, Gift_Cards about 152K) for sentiment, topic modeling, LLM review summarization and recommender exercises.
resources.notes: Load from Hugging Face, e.g. load_dataset('McAuley-Lab/Amazon-Reviews-2023', 'raw_review_All_Beauty', trust_remote_code=True); see https://huggingface.co/datasets/McAuley-Lab/Amazon-Reviews-2023 . The full corpus is about 750 GB, so never download all of it. No license is stated; treat it as research/teaching use. The companion paper ('Bridging Language and Items for Retrieval and Recommendation') covers LLM-era retrieval and recommendation.

resources.title: Yelp Open Dataset
resources.license: Yelp dataset terms (described as for educational use; full terms not reviewed)
resources.summary: A subset of Yelp data for educational use: 150,346 businesses, 6,990,280 reviews and 200,100 photos across 11 metro areas, plus check-ins and business attributes (JSON, 4.35 GB compressed).
resources.wiki_use: Team projects on review text, drivers of star ratings and local-business analytics. Give students a pre-filtered city or category subset.
resources.notes: For a ready-made sentiment benchmark, use Yelp/yelp_review_full on Hugging Face: 700K reviews (650K train/50K test) labeled 1 to 5 stars, 323 MB, license 'other' under the Yelp agreement: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Yelp/yelp_review_full

resources.title: TweetEval
resources.authors: Barbieri, F.; Camacho-Collados, J.; Espinosa-Anke, L.; Neves, L.
resources.license: Varies by subset (sentiment CC BY 3.0; others undefined); Twitter terms apply
resources.summary: Seven tweet classification tasks (sentiment, emotion, irony, hate, offensive, emoji, stance) across 11 subsets, about 200K rows (14.2 MB) with fixed splits.
resources.wiki_use: Social-media text lab: compare a lexicon method, a pretrained transformer and zero-shot LLM labels on short, informal text.
resources.notes: Paper: arXiv:2010.12421.

resources.title: MovieLens datasets (ml-latest-small, ml-32m)
resources.authors: GroupLens Research (Harper, F. M.; Konstan, J. A.)
resources.license: GroupLens usage license in each README (research-use conditions)
resources.summary: Movie ratings. ml-latest-small has 100,836 ratings from 610 users on 9,742 movies (1 MB). ml-32m has 32M ratings from 200,948 users on 87,585 movies (239 MB, released May 2024).
resources.wiki_use: Collaborative-filtering and recommender-evaluation lab in M7; ml-latest-small fits easily in Colab.
resources.notes: The DOI is the dataset paper: Harper & Konstan (2015), ACM TiiS 5(4). The README calls ml-latest-small a changing development set that is not appropriate for reported research results; check the license conditions before redistributing. 32M page: https://grouplens.org/datasets/movielens/32m/

resources.title: CTR prediction benchmarks: Avazu (Kaggle) and Criteo 1TB Click Logs
resources.license: Avazu: Kaggle competition rules; Criteo Click Logs on Hugging Face: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
resources.summary: Two standard ad click-through datasets. Avazu is the Kaggle competition to predict whether a mobile ad is clicked. Criteo 1TB Click Logs covers 24 days with 13 integer and 26 hashed categorical features and is a larger version of the Kaggle Display Advertising Challenge data.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-prepared subsamples for M7 classification with high-cardinality categoricals (hashing, target encoding, calibration). Too large for raw student download.
resources.notes: Criteo 1TB: https://ailab.criteo.com/download-criteo-1tb-click-logs-dataset/ ; Hugging Face mirror: https://huggingface.co/datasets/criteo/CriteoClickLogs ; Display Advertising Challenge: https://www.kaggle.com/c/criteo-display-ad-challenge . Avazu row counts and file sizes were not visible (page is JS-rendered).

resources.title: Train and ModeCanada choice datasets (R package mlogit)
resources.summary: Train is a Dutch stated-preference survey: respondents chose between two train trips differing in price, time, number of changes and comfort (up to 16 tasks each, wide format). ModeCanada records mode choice among train, air, bus and car in the Ontario-Quebec corridor (long format; 2,779 situations with all four modes available).
resources.wiki_use: Conjoint-style multinomial/mixed logit and willingness-to-pay exercises (Train mimics a two-alternative conjoint).
resources.notes: Python option: xlogit (pip install xlogit; GPU-accelerated mixed logit, MNL, WTP space) uses an electricity-supplier choice dataset (electricity_long.csv) in its quick start: https://xlogit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ . AER datasets were not checked.

resources.title: statsmodels example datasets and Rdatasets (get_rdataset)
resources.license: Rdatasets code GPL-3; data licenses uncertain per maintainer
resources.summary: statsmodels bundles 28 datasets (e.g. modechoice travel choice, grunfeld, fair, randhie), and sm.datasets.get_rdataset() pulls any of the 3,648 CRAN datasets in Rdatasets into pandas.
resources.wiki_use: Zero-setup data for M3 regression drills in Colab. get_rdataset lets Python students use classic R textbook data without installing R.
resources.notes: Rdatasets index: https://vincentarelbundock.github.io/Rdatasets/

resources.title: R for Marketing Research and Analytics: companion data, code and slides
resources.summary: Companion site with updated R code, data files (mostly simulated), classroom slides, exercises and errata. Includes the Chapter 13 choice-based conjoint data (seats, cargo, engine, price; 3,000 choice tasks) and survey/segmentation data.
resources.wiki_use: Ready-made conjoint, segmentation and satisfaction-survey datasets (plain CSVs readable from Python) for M4 in-class activities.
resources.notes: Data index: http://r-marketing.r-forge.r-project.org/data.html (2nd-edition files are a superset of the 1st). The Chapter 13 instructor page: https://r-marketing.r-forge.r-project.org/Instructor/Chapter13/Chapter13-ChapmanFeit.html . Some loads use goo.gl short links, which may break; use the data folder instead.

resources.title: bayesm package datasets (Rossi)
resources.summary: R package for Bayesian marketing models (v3.0-2 on CRAN) that bundles classic marketing data: Bank (credit-card conjoint), Margarine (scanner panel), Cheese (account-level sales and marketing mix), Scotch, Detailing and CustomerSat.
resources.wiki_use: Hierarchical Bayes conjoint (Bank) and brand-choice (Margarine) examples; an instructor anchor and optional student extension.
resources.notes: CRAN: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/bayesm/index.html

resources.title: Dominick's Finer Foods scanner data
resources.authors: Kilts Center for Marketing, Chicago Booth
resources.venue: Kilts Center for Marketing, University of Chicago Booth
resources.license: Academic research use only; acknowledge the Kilts Center
resources.summary: Weekly store-level UPC sales, price, profit margin and deal codes for 29 categories (3,500+ UPCs) from about 100 Chicago-area stores, 1989 to 1994, plus daily customer counts and store demographics. CSV, SAS and Stata.
resources.wiki_use: Price-elasticity and promotion regressions in M3 using one category's movement file (e.g. soft drinks or cereals).
resources.notes: Free direct download. The terms say 'for academic research purposes only' and do not address teaching; confirm classroom use with marketingdata@chicagobooth.edu. The page gives inconsistent coverage lengths ('seven years', 'nine years'). Use the truncated PRICE/PROFIT variables in the CSVs.

resources.title: NielsenIQ Retail Scanner and Consumer Panel data (Kilts Center)
resources.authors: Kilts Center for Marketing, Chicago Booth; NielsenIQ
resources.summary: Consumer Panel (household purchases from 2004, about 40-60K active panelists) and Retail Scanner (weekly store-level price and volume from 2006, 90+ chains, 35-50K stores), available through an institutional subscription.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only background or a faculty/PhD research resource. Not usable for master's team projects under UIUC's eligibility rules.
resources.notes: UIUC has a contract (Consumer Panel, Retail Scanner, PanelView surveys) through DSRS: https://dsrs.illinois.edu/datahub/nielsen . Authorized users are tenured and tenure-track faculty, PhD students and postdocs, on campus, for scholarly use only. Master's students are not listed and classroom use is not addressed.

resources.title: Robyn: Meta's open-source marketing mix modeling package
resources.summary: An automated MMM in R: ridge regression, evolutionary hyperparameter search, adstock/saturation, calibration to lift experiments and budget allocation. Has a beta Python API.
resources.wiki_use: Compare with Meridian and PyMC-Marketing in a 'which MMM would you trust?' discussion, using the R demo script or the Python API notebook.
resources.notes: Year is the release of the Python API beta (Nov 2023). Site: https://facebookexperimental.github.io/Robyn/ . R demo: demo/demo.R. The Python API notebook is robyn_api/robyn_python_notebook.ipynb and needs R installed.

resources.title: Google Meridian simulated geo-level MMM data (geo_all_channels)
resources.summary: Simulated geo-by-week MMM data in CSV, XLSX and xarray-pickle formats. It has five paid channels (impressions and spend), one organic channel, a promo treatment, controls (GQV, competitor sales), population, conversions and revenue per conversion.
resources.wiki_use: Geo-level Bayesian MMM demo in Colab using Meridian's Getting Started notebook, contrasted with Robyn and PyMC-Marketing.
resources.notes: The repo also has demo/ Colab notebooks (e.g. demo/Meridian_Full_Funnel.ipynb) and top-level .agents and skills folders, whose contents were not inspected (listing blocked). The number of geos and weeks was not stated on the page.

resources.title: PyMC-Marketing example data: synthetic MMM and CDNOW CLV
resources.summary: The MMM example notebook builds a synthetic dataset step by step (179 weeks, two channels, events, trend, adstock and saturation) and then recovers the parameters. The repo's data/ folder provides mmm_example.csv and cdnow_transactions.csv for the MMM and CLV quickstarts.
resources.wiki_use: Shows the data-generating process before fitting, which suits 'can the AI-written model recover the known truth?' exercises. Use CDNOW for BG/NBD plus Gamma-Gamma CLV in M4.
resources.notes: The repo ships an LLM coding-assistant skill for MMM workflows (skills/mmm-modeling/SKILL.md), listed at https://tessl.io/registry/skills/github/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/mmm-modeling . It warns about mistakes such as flat priors on saturation. The data/ folder contents are inferred from quickstart code because the listing was blocked.

resources.title: CDNOW and other BTYD datasets (Bruce Hardie)
resources.summary: Small classic datasets for probability models of customer behavior: CDNOW (full, 424 KB zip, and a 1/10 sample), 'Kiwi Bubbles' test-market panel data, cumulative trial data for 19 new products, and a 1995-cohort donation-incidence dataset.
resources.wiki_use: M4 CLV exercise: fit BG/NBD and Gamma-Gamma on CDNOW (2,357 customers, 78 weeks), then compare against RFM heuristics.
resources.notes: No terms of use are stated. A ready CSV used by PyMC-Marketing: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/main/data/cdnow_transactions.csv

resources.title: causaldata (Python, R and Stata package)
resources.summary: Packages the example datasets from The Effect (Huntington-Klein) and Causal Inference: The Mixtape (Cunningham) for pip, CRAN and Stata (Python v0.1.5, Nov 2024).
resources.wiki_use: Load textbook causal-inference datasets in one line to reproduce book examples (DiD, IV, RD, matching) in Colab.
resources.notes: R: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/causaldata/index.html . The PyPI page does not list the datasets. Cunningham's Mixtape (online 2nd ed. at https://mixtape.scunning.com/) uses R and Stata, so this package is the Python route to its data.

resources.title: Reddit Data API and Reddit for Researchers access rules
resources.summary: Reddit's policy: the Data API is rate-limited and bulk export is restricted. Academic research must go through the Reddit for Researchers program, and content may not be used for model training without Reddit's consent.
resources.wiki_use: Required policy reading for M5 social-media analysis. It explains why students should not scrape Reddit or use the API for research projects, and how research access works.
resources.notes: Reddit for Researchers eligibility is not listed; applications go through a support ticket. Requests from hosted-service IP ranges, likely including cloud notebooks, need OAuth or a login. Checked 2026-10-23: access needs an application and approval (Data API app review, or Reddit for Researchers); it is not self-serve sign-up. Don't plan student projects on Reddit data without lead time.

resources.title: Bluesky developer docs and Jetstream
resources.summary: Docs for the open AT Protocol HTTP API and SDKs (official TypeScript and Go; community Python and Dart). Jetstream is a lightweight JSON stream of public network events, filterable by collection or account.
resources.wiki_use: The most practical open source of live social-media text for M5, via the Python SDK. Use Jetstream for prototypes; Bluesky says it is not the right tool for research-grade archives.
resources.notes: Jetstream post: https://docs.bsky.app/blog/jetstream (public instances; events are not signed). Authentication and terms are not on the landing page; review Bluesky's developer guidelines and ethics/IRB considerations before collecting user posts.

resources.title: Stanford Large Network Dataset Collection (SNAP)
resources.summary: Graph datasets including social networks, Amazon co-purchasing graphs with product metadata and reviews (about 548K products), review corpora (BeerAdvocate, RateBeer, Amazon fine foods), Twitter diffusion (higgs-twitter) and Epinions trust networks.
resources.wiki_use: M5 network-analysis lab with networkx: co-purchase centrality, community detection and diffusion.

resources.title: TidyTuesday weekly datasets
resources.summary: A new real-world dataset each week, organized by year and date (2018 to 2026) with a readme and source article for each; Python users join with #PydyTuesday.
resources.wiki_use: Weekly M2 viz warm-ups or a 'pick any TidyTuesday dataset' option for a short assignment; CC0 allows hosting copies on the wiki.
resources.notes: Python resources: github.com/posit-dev/python-tidytuesday-challenge (linked from the README). Download only the selected weeks; the full repo is large.

resources.title: Kaggle Datasets
resources.summary: Hundreds of thousands of community-uploaded datasets with notebooks; each dataset lists its own license.
resources.wiki_use: Discovery source for team-project data. Require students to record the license and provenance, since mirrors often mislabel licenses (see the Instacart CC0 mirror).
resources.notes: The Kaggle API (kaggle datasets download) works from Colab with an API token.

resources.title: Hugging Face Datasets Hub
resources.summary: Over 1.1 million datasets (as of this check), loadable with the datasets library; the main source for text, review and sentiment data.
resources.wiki_use: Default source for M5 text datasets; teach load_dataset() and reading dataset cards for license and provenance.

resources.title: Google Dataset Search
resources.summary: Search engine over datasets described with schema.org metadata across repositories; supports site: filters (e.g. site:huggingface.co).
resources.wiki_use: Teach students how to find and vet data for team projects.
resources.notes: data.world's open community, often listed with these aggregators, was retired on July 13, 2026 (its datasets are no longer downloadable), so it is omitted.

resources.title: Python for Data Analysis, 3rd Edition (Open Access)
resources.license: Online text free to read, not to be copied; code examples MIT
resources.summary: The pandas creator's guide to data wrangling with pandas, NumPy and Jupyter. The full 3rd edition is free to read online.
resources.wiki_use: Assigned reading for M1-M2 (pandas basics, groupby, time series). Link to chapters from the wiki rather than copying text.

resources.title: Python Data Science Handbook
resources.summary: The full book as Jupyter notebooks, covering IPython, NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib and scikit-learn (including k-means and Gaussian mixture clustering).
resources.wiki_use: Embed or launch notebooks for M4 clustering and M7 scikit-learn workflows.
resources.notes: The repo also has notebooks_v1 and notebooks_v2 folders (v2 presumably matches the 2nd edition; not confirmed). Edition years were not verified.

resources.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python (ISLP)
resources.authors: James, G.; Witten, D.; Hastie, T.; Tibshirani, R.; Taylor, J.
resources.summary: The standard intro to regression, classification, resampling, regularization, trees, SVMs, deep learning and unsupervised learning, now with Python labs. The PDF is a free download.
resources.wiki_use: Core reading for M3 (regression) and M7 (prediction); the ISLP labs can be assigned as runnable notebooks.
resources.notes: Labs repo v2.2.2 targets Python 3.12. Its README mentions Codespaces and uv, not Colab.

resources.title: Think Stats, 3rd Edition
resources.license: Creative Commons, attribution and non-commercial (book); repo MIT
resources.summary: Notebook-first intro to exploratory data analysis, distributions, hypothesis testing and regression in Python. Chapters 1-14 each open in Colab.
resources.wiki_use: Statistics refresher for students weak on inference before M3 and M6; chapters can be linked as Colab notebooks.
resources.notes: The page footer says (c) 2023; the 3rd-edition publication year was not confirmed.

resources.title: Think Python, 3rd Edition
resources.summary: Beginner Python textbook with every chapter (1-19) as a Colab notebook. Each chapter ends with suggestions for using ChatGPT and Colab AI to learn more and get help with exercises.
resources.wiki_use: M1 primer for non-programmers. Its end-of-chapter AI-assistant prompts model a 'learn with AI, verify yourself' habit.

resources.subtopic: Python for economics and data science
resources.title: QuantEcon DataScience: Introduction to Economic Modeling and Data Science
resources.authors: Coleman, C.; Lyon, S.; Perla, J.
resources.summary: A Python course running from basics through pandas, visualization, regression and classification to applications (ML in economics, networks, text analysis, heterogeneous effects), with one-click Colab launch.
resources.wiki_use: Ready-made notebooks to adapt (CC BY-SA permits remixing with attribution and share-alike) for M1-M3 and the M5 text and network applications.
resources.notes: Other QuantEcon series (https://quantecon.org/lectures/) are more macro- and theory-oriented: Python Programming for Economics and Finance (https://python-programming.quantecon.org/), A First Course in Quantitative Economics with Python (https://intro.quantecon.org/), and Intermediate (https://python.quantecon.org/).

resources.title: Data Science for Economists (EC 607 lecture notes)
resources.summary: PhD lecture notes on Git/GitHub, the shell, R, tidyverse/data.table wrangling, web scraping and APIs, regression, spatial analysis, parallel computing, Docker, cloud computing, databases and Spark.
resources.wiki_use: Borrow the Git/GitHub and shell lectures for the GitHub-based project workflow. The rest is R-based, so use it selectively.

resources.title: Computational and Inferential Thinking: The Foundations of Data Science, 2nd ed. (Berkeley Data 8)
resources.authors: Adhikari, A.; DeNero, J.; Wagner, D.
resources.summary: Data 8 textbook covering causality and experiments, Python tables and visualization, sampling, hypothesis testing, comparing two samples (A/B tests), estimation, regression inference and classification.
resources.wiki_use: A gentle, simulation-based treatment of A/B testing and permutation tests for non-CS students in M6.
resources.notes: Uses Berkeley's own 'datascience' Tables library rather than pandas; translate examples for consistency.

resources.title: Data 100 Course Notes: Principles and Techniques of Data Science
resources.summary: Fall 2025 notes on pandas EDA, regex, visualization, sampling, linear models, gradient descent, feature engineering, cross-validation and regularization, the bootstrap, logistic regression, clustering and PCA.
resources.wiki_use: Concise readings to pair with modules; the regex and feature-engineering notes fit M5 and M7.

resources.title: Kaggle Learn micro-courses
resources.summary: Free, short, hands-on courses that run in Kaggle notebooks, covering Python, data viz, pandas, machine learning and more.
resources.wiki_use: Pre-course or remedial assignments (e.g. Python, Pandas, Intro to ML) for students to finish before in-class labs.
resources.notes: The page is JS-rendered, so the full course list and certificate details were not retrieved. The Pandas course was verified at https://www.kaggle.com/learn/pandas .

resources.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
resources.summary: Free top-down deep learning course (Part 1, 2022 edition) covering vision, NLP, tabular data, collaborative filtering, random forests and deployment with PyTorch, fastai and Hugging Face. Runs on Kaggle Notebooks.
resources.wiki_use: Optional extension for students who want deep-learning or recommender depth in M7 projects.

resources.title: Coding for Economists
resources.summary: Python book for economists covering reproducible workflow (Quarto, version control), data handling, visualization (matplotlib, seaborn, lets-plot, plotnine), regression and diagnostics, causal inference, text/regex/NLP, ML and time series.
resources.wiki_use: Reference for workflow, regression and causal chapters. The MIT license lets you adapt pages directly into the wiki.

resources.title: Introduction to Python for Econometrics, Statistics and Numerical Analysis
resources.summary: Free PDF notes taking beginners through Python, NumPy, SciPy, matplotlib and pandas, with econometric examples (GJR-GARCH, Fama-MacBeth, GMM).
resources.wiki_use: Instructor reference and optional reading for students who want rigorous numerical Python. It is finance-econometrics oriented.
resources.notes: Edition labeling on the page is inconsistent (4th edition 2021 vs 'fifth edition'). Mini-course: https://www.kevinsheppard.com/teaching/python/course/

resources.title: Causal Inference for the Brave and True
resources.summary: Free Python book on potential outcomes, causal graphs, randomized experiments, IV, matching and propensity scores, DiD, synthetic control, RD and heterogeneous effects/meta-learners, with tech-industry applications.
resources.wiki_use: Core M6 reading. Its notebooks and data can be embedded or adapted.

resources.title: The Effect: An Introduction to Research Design and Causality
resources.summary: Free online textbook on causal research design (causal diagrams, controls, matching, DiD, IV, RD and more), with code examples in R, Stata and Python.
resources.wiki_use: Accessible M6 conceptual reading. Pair it with the causaldata package so students run the examples in Colab.
resources.notes: The author plans to keep the web version free. Cunningham's 'Causal Inference: The Mixtape' (online 2nd edition, https://mixtape.scunning.com/, R and Stata) is a companion option.

resources.title: Applied Causal Inference Powered by ML and AI
resources.authors: Chernozhukov, V.; Hansen, C.; Kallus, N.; Spindler, M.; Syrgkanis, V.
resources.summary: Free graduate-level textbook on double/debiased machine learning and causal ML for treatment effects, with Python and R labs.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor anchor and optional reading for students using ML for causal estimation (DML, heterogeneous effects).
resources.notes: The landing page does not state a year or license, and the lab notebook links are not on that page.

resources.title: Hugging Face LLM Course
resources.summary: Free course on transformers and LLMs: pretrained models, fine-tuning, the Datasets and Tokenizers libraries, classic NLP tasks, demos, dataset curation, LLM fine-tuning and reasoning models.
resources.wiki_use: Chapters 1-2 and the Datasets chapter support M5 sentiment and text classification with pretrained models in Colab.

resources.title: Python for Everybody (PY4E)
resources.summary: Free, openly licensed beginner Python course with a book, lectures and autograded assignments, built for reuse by other instructors (Common Cartridge export, LTI).
resources.wiki_use: Remedial Python track for students with no programming background. CC BY allows remixing into the wiki.

resources.title: Data Science DISCOVERY (University of Illinois)
resources.summary: Free Illinois resource (the basis of STAT/CS/IS 107) covering Python data science basics, EDA, simulation and distributions, probability, regression and clustering, and hypothesis testing.
resources.wiki_use: A campus-made intro some students may already know; link it for refreshers and to connect with UIUC data science offerings.
resources.notes: License not stated.

resources.title: Fundamentals of Data Visualization
resources.summary: Free online guide to choosing and designing figures: aesthetics, color, amounts, distributions, proportions, associations, time series, uncertainty, figure design and telling a story with figures.
resources.wiki_use: M2 reading on chart choice and design, paired with the Pyramid Principle for communicating results. The text is software-agnostic.

resources.title: Speech and Language Processing, 3rd ed. draft
resources.summary: Free draft (Aug 19, 2026 release) of the standard NLP textbook. It now opens with a volume on large language models (transformers, pretraining, post-training) and includes chapters on embeddings and on sentiment and affect lexicons.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor background, plus selective student readings on embeddings and sentiment lexicons for M5.

resources.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education
resources.summary: MIT's short course on the shell, command-line environment, Git, development tools, debugging, packaging and code quality. The January 2026 edition adds an 'Agentic Coding' lecture and folds AI tools into every lecture.
resources.wiki_use: Assign the Git and Agentic Coding lectures before the team project; a model for teaching AI coding tools alongside fundamentals.

resources.section: Marketing analytics books and peer courses
resources.title: Python for Marketing Research and Analytics
resources.authors: Schwarz, J. S.; Chapman, C.; Feit, E. M.
resources.summary: The Python edition of Chapman and Feit's marketing-research text. All analyses are Colab notebooks with chapter data files and a pip-installable helper package.
resources.wiki_use: Closest-fit textbook for the course. Embed its Colab notebooks and data for M2-M4 activities; the code is Apache-2.0, so it can be adapted.
resources.notes: Springer page: https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-49720-0 (likely in UIUC's SpringerLink holdings; not checked). The chapter list was not verified; topics are expected to mirror the R edition (regression, segmentation, choice modeling).

resources.section: Marketing analytics books and peer courses
resources.subtopic: Marketing analytics in Python and R
resources.title: Hands-On Data Science for Marketing (code repository)
resources.summary: MIT-licensed code for a 12-chapter Packt book that works marketing use cases in parallel Python and R.
resources.wiki_use: Source of short marketing-specific Python examples to adapt into in-class activities. The book itself is paid.
resources.notes: Chapter topics (recalled as KPIs, engagement, CLV, segmentation, churn, A/B testing) and the publication year were not verified; it requires Python >= 3.6, so expect some version drift.

resources.section: Marketing analytics books and peer courses
resources.title: Dealing with Data (NYU teaching notebooks)
resources.summary: Notebooks from NYU classes that teach programming for data science to non-CS majors through live examples: pandas, web APIs, regex, scraping, time series, maps, text mining/NLP, visualization, network analysis, crowdsourcing and predictive modeling.
resources.wiki_use: A model for teaching non-CS business students. Borrow the text-mining and network notebooks for M5, with attribution and non-commercial use.

resources.section: Marketing analytics books and peer courses
resources.title: Business Data Science: code and examples
resources.summary: R scripts, data (examples/) and notebooks accompanying the book Business Data Science.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor reference for business-framed regression, regularization and causal examples; the datasets in examples/ can be reused in Python.
resources.notes: No license is shown. The publisher (McGraw Hill, 2019) and the book's origin in Taddy's Chicago Booth course are from memory; verify.

resources.section: Marketing analytics books and peer courses
resources.title: Customer Analytics (Wharton, Coursera)
resources.authors: Bradlow, E.; Fader, P.; Iyengar, R.; et al.
resources.summary: Introductory course in Wharton's Business Analytics Specialization on descriptive, predictive (CLV, customer-based corporate valuation) and prescriptive customer analytics, with examples from Amazon, Google and Starbucks.
resources.wiki_use: Optional video background on CLV and customer-centric valuation for M4. It is not Python-based.

resources.section: Marketing analytics books and peer courses
resources.title: pyrsm and Radiant: business-analytics teaching tools from UCSD Rady
resources.venue: PyPI; Rady School of Management, UC San Diego
resources.license: AGPL-3.0 (pyrsm); Radiant AGPLv3 with CC-licensed docs
resources.summary: pyrsm is the Python package used in Rady's MSBA for basic tests, linear/logistic regression, ML models and EDA. Its R sibling Radiant is a browser-based Shiny app with conjoint, brand maps, clustering, collaborative filtering and experimental-design modules.
resources.wiki_use: Shows how a peer MSBA program wraps model output for business students. The Radiant docs show marketing-analytics workflows (conjoint, perceptual maps).
resources.notes: Radiant docs: https://radiant-rstats.github.io/docs/ . AGPL matters if modified code is redistributed.

resources.section: Marketing analytics books and peer courses
resources.title: Ad response tutorial: last-click attribution, experiments, MMM and attribution models
resources.summary: Workshop materials (R code, LaTeX slides, handout) that apply last-click attribution, experiments, marketing-mix models and attribution models to the same synthetic advertising data, including the data preparation.
resources.wiki_use: Template for an M6/M8 activity: students port the R analysis to Python with AI help and compare the estimates across methods.
resources.notes: No license file was seen, so link to it rather than copying.

resources.section: Marketing analytics books and peer courses
resources.title: Marketing Science Institute library (free working papers)
resources.summary: MSI offers free access to its working papers, plus webinars in which academics and practitioners present current marketing research. Some content is members-only.
resources.wiki_use: Source of current-topics readings for M8. No dedicated teaching-resource section was found.
resources.notes: AMA teaching resources could not be verified (the target page did not load).

resources.section: Marketing analytics books and peer courses
resources.title: Darden Business Publishing (cases, simulations, course packs)
resources.authors: University of Virginia Darden School of Business
resources.summary: Store for cases, technical notes, exercises and simulations (including a digital-marketing attribution simulation), with a course-pack builder and free educator resources.
resources.wiki_use: Source of paid marketing-analytics cases with data, if the budget allows a per-student fee.
resources.notes: Venkatesan, Farris & Wilcox's book of Darden marketing-analytics cases with data sets ('Cutting-Edge Marketing Analytics') could not be verified because the publisher pages failed to load. Harvard Business Publishing Education (https://hbsp.harvard.edu/cases/) loads only with JavaScript, so its data cases were not checked.

resources.title: AI Python for Beginners
resources.summary: 11.5-hour beginner course on Python basics, files and CSVs, matplotlib, web scraping, packages and APIs. A built-in AI assistant helps learners write, test and debug code.
resources.wiki_use: Pre-course onboarding for students new to Python that introduces AI-assisted coding from day one.
resources.notes: Free during the platform beta; a certificate requires a PRO membership.

resources.title: Modern Statistics: A Computer-Based Approach with Python
resources.authors: Kenett, R.; Zacks, S.; Gedeck, P.
resources.summary: Springer textbook on statistics with Python, with the companion mistat package (MIT) and a public repository of code and exercise solutions.
resources.wiki_use: Optional statistics reference with worked Python solutions; its industrial-statistics flavor makes it a secondary pick behind ISLP and Think Stats.
resources.notes: mistat on PyPI (MIT): https://pypi.org/project/mistat/ . The repository's license is not visible. A companion volume, Industrial Statistics, came out in 2023. Likely available through UIUC SpringerLink (not checked).

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: FlowingData (Nathan Yau)
resources.summary: Nathan Yau's long-running site on visualization and statistics: free posts that collect and critique notable charts, plus step-by-step tutorials (mostly R, some Python and JavaScript) and the 'Process' newsletter, which are for paying members.
resources.wiki_use: Source of strong current examples for an M2 'chart critique' activity. Link to the posts; the members-only tutorials cannot be redistributed.
resources.notes: Tutorials are members-only (https://flowingdata.com/membership/). Nothing was downloaded.

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: Visualize This: The FlowingData Guide to Design, Visualization, and Statistics (2nd ed.)
resources.summary: Revised second edition (2024) of Yau's practical guide to turning data into charts, covering design choices, chart types for time, proportions, relationships and space, and tools from spreadsheets to R and JavaScript.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor reference and optional student reading for M2. Check whether the UIUC library offers an e-book licence.
resources.notes: Commercial book with no open code repository found; link only.

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: Visual Vocabulary (Financial Times chart-doctor)
resources.summary: The FT's one-page poster that organizes chart types by the relationship you want to show (deviation, correlation, ranking, distribution, change over time, part-to-whole, magnitude, spatial, flow).
resources.wiki_use: M2 reference for choosing a display from the analytical question. Preserve attribution and the MIT license when reproducing the poster.

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: Scientific Visualization: Python + Matplotlib (open-access book and code)
resources.license: BSD-2-Clause (code); CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (book), separately specified in LICENSE.txt
resources.summary: Open-access book on making publication-quality figures with Matplotlib (anatomy of a figure, colors, typography, layout, animation, common pitfalls), with the full source code for every figure.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor resource for polishing the course's own figures, and a source of 'make this chart better' exercises. The code folder is saved locally.
resources.notes: The book PDF was not downloaded. LICENSE.txt separately licenses code under BSD-2-Clause and book material under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The original license file is retained.

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: Matplotlib cheatsheets and handouts (source)
resources.summary: Source for the official Matplotlib cheatsheets and beginner, intermediate and tips handouts.
resources.wiki_use: Link the rendered PDFs (matplotlib.org/cheatsheets) from the wiki; the saved source lets you rebuild or adapt them.

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: Matplotlib cheat sheet (Rougier)
resources.summary: Compact cheat sheet covering Matplotlib's figure anatomy, styles, colormaps and annotation options, with the scripts that generate it.
resources.wiki_use: Optional quick reference alongside the official cheatsheets.

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: seaborn user-guide tutorial notebooks
resources.summary: The notebooks behind seaborn's official user guide: the objects interface, distributions, relational and categorical plots, regression plots, multi-plot grids, aesthetics and color palettes.
resources.wiki_use: Core M2 lab material in the library students will use most. Adapt sections into wiki exercises rather than linking the whole guide.

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: Altair tutorial notebooks (Exploratory Data Visualization with Altair)
resources.summary: Short, sequenced notebooks introducing declarative visualization with Altair: simple charts, binning and aggregation, compound charts, interactivity and exploration.
resources.wiki_use: Altair renders in the browser, so these suit interactive wiki pages. Pairs with the UW visualization curriculum already in this folder.
resources.notes: The repository identifies the tutorial as PyCon 2018 and uses older selection APIs. The original course adaptation uses Altair 5.5.0; see visualization_charts.py.

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: Bokeh tutorial notebooks
resources.summary: Official 15-notebook Bokeh tutorial on interactive web plots: basic plots, styling, layouts, interactions, data sources and widgets.
resources.wiki_use: Option for interactive dashboards on the wiki or in final-project blogs.

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: HoloViz tutorial (hvPlot, Panel, HoloViews)
resources.summary: Tutorial notebooks showing how to go from pandas to interactive plots with one-line hvPlot calls and build simple dashboards with Panel.
resources.wiki_use: Optional route to interactive dashboards for teams that want one in the final project.
resources.notes: Some notebooks download example data on first run.

resources.section: Data visualization: practitioners, guides and code
resources.title: Urban Institute Data Visualization Style Guide (source)
resources.summary: Source for one of the best-known public data-visualization style guides: chart types, colors, typography, labels and accessibility rules for a research organization.
resources.wiki_use: Reference for chart conventions, labels, and accessibility. Graded requirements belong in released assignment briefs. Link to the published guide.
