resources.notes: The project page links the Patterns 2023 paper and keeps a table (updated May 2024) of 41 papers across 30 fields that document leakage errors, which together affect 648 papers.

resources.title: Data Leakage in Notebooks: Static Detection and Better Processes
resources.authors: Yang, C.; Brower-Sinning, R. A.; Lewis, G. A.; Kästner, C.
resources.summary: A static-analysis tool that detects common train/test leakage patterns in data-science notebooks. Leakage turns out to be widespread across more than 100,000 public notebooks, and the paper discusses processes to prevent it.
resources.wiki_use: Evidence that leakage is the default failure in notebook code, which is also what LLMs learn from. Motivates the course rule: always split first and use a Pipeline.
resources.notes: arXiv lists no journal reference. I believe it appeared at ASE 2022, but that venue is unverified.

resources.title: AutoGluon Tabular: Quick Start
resources.summary: Three lines of code (TabularPredictor.fit) train and stack many models on a tabular dataset. It comes with a ready Colab notebook.
resources.wiki_use: Benchmark exercise: compare AutoGluon against the student's hand-tuned XGBoost on the same holdout, then discuss what AutoML can't do (framing the problem, leakage, the business metric).
resources.notes: The repo README also lists the MLZero multi-agent AutoML paper (arXiv 2505.13941) and the TabArena benchmark (arXiv 2506.16791), both NeurIPS 2025.

resources.title: TabPFN: Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model
resources.authors: Hollmann, N.; et al. (Prior Labs / University of Freiburg)
resources.license: Apache-2.0 (code); model weights under separate, partly non-commercial licenses
resources.summary: A pretrained transformer that does classification and regression on small tabular datasets in one forward pass, with no tuning, through a scikit-learn-style API. It is often competitive with tuned boosting.
resources.wiki_use: Shows where 'foundation models' are heading for tabular marketing data. Students drop TabPFNClassifier into their churn pipeline and compare it with XGBoost.
resources.notes: The Nature page fetch failed; the DOI and title come from the GitHub README. TabPFN-2.5 and later weights are non-commercial (fine for class use). It needs a GPU for larger data.

resources.title: GEO: Generative Engine Optimization
resources.authors: Aggarwal, P.; Murahari, V.; Rajpurohit, T.; Kalyan, A.; Narasimhan, K.; Deshpande, A.
resources.venue: arXiv 2311.09735 (v3, June 2024); KDD 2024 per course brief (venue not verified)
resources.summary: Defines generative engine optimization: making content visible in LLM-generated search answers. Introduces GEO-bench (10K queries) and shows that strategies such as adding citations, quotes and statistics can raise visibility by up to 40%.
resources.wiki_use: The anchor reading for 'SEO becomes GEO'. Students rewrite a product page with GEO tactics and test their visibility in an LLM answer engine.
resources.notes: The ACM DL page (KDD) could not be fetched, and the project page cites the work only as arXiv. GEO-bench is at huggingface.co/datasets/GEO-optim/geo-bench.

resources.title: Frontiers: Supporting Content Marketing with Natural Language Generation
resources.authors: Reisenbichler, M.; Reutterer, T.; Schweidel, D. A.; Dan, D.
resources.summary: Machine-drafted, human-edited SEO landing-page copy is nearly indistinguishable from expert copy, and in field experiments it ranks better in search at much lower cost.
resources.wiki_use: Evidence-based case for 'human-in-the-loop' GenAI content, which pairs with GEO as the 'before and after' of LLM search.

resources.title: Buy it in ChatGPT: Instant Checkout and the Agentic Commerce Protocol
resources.summary: OpenAI's launch of in-chat purchasing (starting with US Etsy sellers, Shopify planned) and the open Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP), co-developed with Stripe, in which merchants stay merchant of record.
resources.wiki_use: Primary source for the agentic-commerce lecture. Ask what happens to brand choice, search ads and retail media when an AI agent does the shopping.
resources.notes: Developer docs are at developers.openai.com/commerce. The ACP license (Apache 2.0) is stated on agenticcommerce.dev; I did not fetch the GitHub repo itself.

resources.title: Powering AI commerce with the new Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
resources.summary: Google's open protocol for AI agents to initiate payments, using signed 'Intent' and 'Cart' mandates as an audit trail. More than 60 partners (Mastercard, AmEx, PayPal, Adyen, Coinbase and others) back it, and it works as an extension of A2A alongside MCP.
resources.wiki_use: Compare with OpenAI's ACP: who controls the customer relationship and the data when agents buy?
resources.notes: The repo is linked as goo.gle/ap2; no direct GitHub URL was verified, and the license was not stated.

resources.title: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
resources.authors: UCP Authors (co-developed by Google, Shopify and others)
resources.summary: An open standard covering the whole agentic shopping flow (discovery, checkout, post-purchase) between platforms, agents and businesses. It builds on AP2 for payments.
resources.wiki_use: A 2026 snapshot of the competing agentic-commerce standards (ACP vs AP2/UCP) for a short comparison table on the wiki.
resources.notes: The announcement date is not stated on the site. The year 2026 comes from the copyright and the lodging draft. The site lists Amazon, Microsoft and Stripe among co-developers; check this before citing.

resources.title: When AI Guides the Shopping Journey
resources.summary: Mixed-method study (450+ digital ethnographies plus a survey of 600 US consumers). Nearly 40% of US shoppers use AI when shopping. AI reshapes rather than shortens the path to purchase, and trust friction is common.
resources.wiki_use: Consumer-side evidence to pair with the agentic-commerce protocols, and a source of discussion stats.
resources.notes: Download terms (free or registration) were not stated.

resources.title: App Tracking Transparency (framework documentation)
resources.summary: Apple's official documentation for the ATT permission that apps must request before tracking users across other companies' apps and sites or accessing the IDFA. It was introduced with iOS 14.5.
resources.wiki_use: Primary source for the ATT shock to mobile ad targeting and attribution, to pair with a discussion of how platforms shifted to modeled conversions and MMM.
resources.notes: The page is JavaScript-rendered, so the fetch returned only metadata. The iOS 14.5 and 2021 dates are standard knowledge, not quoted from the page. No academic ATT study was verified in this pass (search budget ran out).

resources.title: IAB Tech Lab Standards: Data Clean Rooms Guidance, PAIR, and ADMaP
resources.authors: IAB Tech Lab (Addressability and PETs Working Group)
resources.summary: Industry standards index listing the Data Clean Rooms Guidance (v1.0, July 2024), PAIR for privacy-safe advertiser-publisher ID matching in clean rooms (2024), and ADMaP for sharing conversion data with private set intersection or TEEs (February 2025).
resources.wiki_use: Instructor background and a short explainer on how clean rooms let a brand and a retailer join first-party data without exchanging it.
resources.notes: The fetched index page did not expose deep links to each standard. For a concrete vendor example, AWS Clean Rooms (aws.amazon.com/clean-rooms/, verified) supports SQL and PySpark analyses, differential privacy and ML on partner data.

resources.title: Retail Media ROAS Demystified: Understanding Your Brand's ROAS
resources.authors: Nelson, D. T.; Bante, K.; Gordon, B. R.; Anderson, E. T.; Dantzinger, L.; Armor, S.
resources.venue: Ovative Group with Albertsons Media Collective and Kellogg School of Management (May 15, 2025)
resources.summary: Analyzes 573 Albertsons Media Collective campaigns to show how retail-media-network ROAS methods differ and how much reported results shift with methodology. Ends with questions advertisers should ask RMNs.
resources.wiki_use: Retail-media case reading (with Kellogg co-authors Gordon and Anderson). Students explain why platform-reported ROAS and incremental ROAS differ.
resources.notes: The PDF link was given on the fetched page; I did not fetch the PDF itself.

resources.title: The Commerce Media Connection Gap: Why the Next Phase of Growth Depends on the Cohesion of the Ecosystem
resources.summary: Survey of 281 brands, agencies and RMNs in six countries (fieldwork July to August 2026). Reporting is the least connected function, only 14% get unified cross-channel reporting, and 46% of brands say proven incremental ROI would unlock more spend.
resources.wiki_use: A very current snapshot of retail-media pain points (fragmentation, measurement) for the M8 discussion.
resources.notes: The report contains no RMN spend figures. For market size, see the IAB/PwC Internet Advertising Revenue Report FY2025 (iab.com/insights/internet-advertising-revenue-report-full-year-2025/, verified; about $300B in US internet ad revenue in 2025, +13.9%; key takeaways need a free IAB account).

resources.title: 2025 Creator Economy Ad Spend & Strategy Report
resources.summary: US creator ad spend projected at $37B in 2025 (+26% year over year, about 4x faster than overall media), $44B expected in 2026. 48% of buyers call creators a 'must buy', and 3 in 4 brands use or plan AI for creator marketing.
resources.wiki_use: Size-of-market slide and discussion: why creator measurement and standards lag, linked to M5 social media analysis.
resources.notes: The summary page is public and the full PDF is downloadable from it. The page was modified June 2026.

resources.title: Algorithmic Bias? An Empirical Study of Apparent Gender-Based Discrimination in the Display of STEM Career Ads
resources.summary: A gender-neutral STEM job ad was shown to fewer women because younger women are a more expensive audience. Cost-minimizing delivery produced the apparent bias, and the pattern held across platforms.
resources.wiki_use: Core case for algorithmic bias arising from market mechanics rather than intent, discussed alongside Ali et al. (2019).

resources.title: Discrimination through optimization: How Facebook's ad delivery can lead to skewed outcomes
resources.authors: Ali, M.; Sapiezynski, P.; Bogen, M.; Korolova, A.; Mislove, A.; Rieke, A.
resources.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction (CSCW 2019); arXiv 1904.02095
resources.summary: Paired ad experiments show that Facebook's delivery optimization skews employment and housing ads by gender and race even with neutral targeting, driven by budget effects and the platform's predicted relevance of the ad content.
resources.wiki_use: Pair with Lambrecht and Tucker: one shows a market-cost mechanism, the other a platform-prediction mechanism. Good for a debate on who is accountable.
resources.notes: The venue (PACM HCI/CSCW) is inferred from the ACM DOI listed on arXiv.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Pricing, and Collusion
resources.authors: Calvano, E.; Calzolari, G.; Denicolò, V.; Pastorello, S.
resources.summary: Q-learning pricing algorithms in simulated oligopolies learn to sustain supra-competitive prices with punishment strategies, without communicating.
resources.wiki_use: Background for the algorithmic-pricing discussion (RealPage-style cases). Present the key figure and intuition rather than assigning the full paper.
resources.notes: Empirical complement: Brown & MacKay (2023), 'Competition in Pricing Algorithms', AEJ: Microeconomics 15(2): 109-56, doi 10.1257/mic.20210158 (aeaweb page verified). It shows that simple rival-responsive pricing algorithms at online retailers can raise prices.

resources.title: The state of AI in 2026: On the road to ROI
resources.authors: Tinkoff, D.; Van der Veken, L.; Chui, M.; Balakrishnan, T. (McKinsey / QuantumBlack)
resources.summary: McKinsey's annual global AI survey. Agent scaling is concentrated in large firms (40% vs 22%), consumer and retail firms most often use agents in marketing and sales, and marketing and sales is where respondents most often report AI-driven revenue gains.
resources.wiki_use: Opening reading for M8 with stats for the 'AI in marketing practice' slide. A 31-page PDF is downloadable.
resources.notes: The 2025 edition is listed on the same page as a previous report. For a value estimate, see McKinsey (2023) 'The economic potential of generative AI' (verified): marketing productivity gains of 5-15% of marketing spend.

resources.title: Exploring Strategic Insights From Gartner's 2026 CMO Spend Survey (webinar)
resources.summary: Gartner's annual survey of CMO budgets: how 2026 budgets are shifting across channels and programs, and how AI is changing marketing capabilities and investment.
resources.wiki_use: Budget benchmark (marketing spend as a share of revenue, channel mix) for the opening of M8. The instructor can watch it and pull two or three headline numbers.
resources.notes: The public page is a free on-demand webinar (work email registration). The full survey report is usually for Gartner clients only. No headline numbers were visible on the page.

resources.title: The 2026 AI Index Report
resources.summary: Annual data-driven report on AI in nine chapters: R&D, technical performance, responsible AI, economy, science, medicine, education, policy and public opinion. It links a full PDF and public data.
resources.wiki_use: Use the Economy and Public Opinion chapters for M8, and the public data folder as an M2 visualization exercise dataset.
resources.notes: The release date and license were not stated on the page. The data is on a public Google Drive folder.

resources.title: Anthropic Economic Index
resources.license: Data CC-BY; code MIT (per dataset card)
resources.summary: Privacy-preserving data on how people use Claude across occupations (O*NET tasks), US states and countries, including automation-vs-augmentation shares. Releases run from February 2025 to June 2026.
resources.wiki_use: Real dataset for a short in-class exercise on which marketing and sales tasks are being automated vs augmented, using the M2 visualization tools.
resources.notes: The full HF dataset is 763 MB, so download only the needed release folder (for example 2026-06-26). The main page was last updated June 26, 2026.

resources.title: One Useful Thing
resources.summary: Ethan Mollick's newsletter on the practical implications of AI for work and education (488K+ subscribers), with frequent hands-on comparisons of frontier models.
resources.wiki_use: Weekly 'stay current' link on the wiki. Individual posts work as short discussion readings on AI-assisted analysis.
resources.notes: Free or paid status was not stated on the page. Most posts are free.

resources.title: The Artificial Intelligence Show
resources.authors: Roetzer, P.; Kaput, M. (Marketing AI Institute / SmarterX)
resources.summary: A weekly (Tuesday) podcast, started in 2021 by the Marketing AI Institute founders, covering AI news and practical guidance for marketers and business careers.
resources.wiki_use: Optional weekly listening, and students can pick an episode to summarize in a short reflection.
resources.notes: marketingaiinstitute.com/podcast-showcase now redirects to podcast.smarterx.ai.

resources.title: AdExchanger (AdExchanger Daily newsletter; AdExchanger Talks podcast)
resources.summary: News and analysis on data-driven marketing: privacy, measurement, commerce and retail media, and ad tech, with a free weekday newsletter and podcasts (AdExchanger Talks, The Big Story, Inside the Stack).
resources.wiki_use: Best single feed for following cookies, clean rooms, MMM and retail media during the semester.
resources.notes: Some articles may be paywalled. Marketing Brew (marketingbrew.com, Morning Brew, weekday newsletter; verified) is a lighter, free alternative.

resources.title: Simon Willison's Weblog
resources.summary: Very frequent, hands-on posts on new LLM releases, coding agents, 'vibe coding', prompt injection and security, and practical tools (LLM CLI, Datasette).
resources.wiki_use: The go-to 'staying current' source for the course's AI-assisted coding emphasis, and for spotting agent failure modes and security risks.
resources.notes: The blog is free. A $10/month curated email briefing is optional.

resources.section: Text analysis in marketing: anchor papers
resources.title: What Makes Online Content Viral?
resources.summary: Codes about 7,000 New York Times articles for emotion with automated sentiment tools and human raters, then models which ones reach the most-emailed list. High-arousal emotions (awe, anger, anxiety) drive sharing more than positivity alone.
resources.wiki_use: Classic M5 example of turning text into variables and regressing an outcome on them. Students can replicate the logic with LLM-coded emotions on the MBA 542 Substack dataset.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 2 reading list.

resources.section: Text analysis in marketing: anchor papers
resources.title: Happiness Begets Money: Emotion and Engagement in Live Streaming
resources.authors: Lin, Y.; Yao, D.; Chen, X.
resources.summary: Uses deep-learning facial-emotion detection on live-stream video to show that broadcaster happiness raises viewer engagement and tipping.
resources.wiki_use: Shows content analysis extending beyond text to video and emotion signals; a good 'where this is heading' reading for M5.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 3 reading list.

resources.section: Text analysis in marketing: anchor papers
resources.title: Visual Listening In: Extracting Brand Image Portrayed on Social Media
resources.authors: Liu, L.; Dzyabura, D.; Mizik, N.
resources.summary: Trains image classifiers on consumer-posted Instagram photos to measure how brands are portrayed on attributes such as glamorous or rugged, and validates the measures against survey-based brand perceptions.
resources.wiki_use: Anchor for extending M5 content analysis from text to images; pairs with today's multimodal LLMs as a cheaper labelling route.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 6 (visual listening) reading list. The open-access link is a working-paper version.

resources.title: Word of Mouth and Interpersonal Communication: A Review and Directions for Future Research
resources.summary: Review of why people share word of mouth (impression management, emotion regulation, information acquisition, social bonding, persuasion) and how sharing shapes the sender and receiver.
resources.wiki_use: Background reading for the social-media analytics part of M5.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 2 reading list.

resources.title: Online Influencer Marketing
resources.authors: Leung, F. F.; Gu, F. F.; Palmatier, R. W.
resources.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science 50(2), 226–251
resources.summary: Integrative review and framework for influencer marketing: influencer, follower, content and brand factors and how they drive engagement and sales. Won the 2022 JAMS Sheth Foundation Best Paper Award.
resources.wiki_use: Framework reading for influencer analytics; pairs with the MBA 542 TikTok transcript exercise, in which an LLM scores expertise and authenticity cues.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 3 reading list. Distinct from the Leung et al. (2022) Journal of Marketing paper on influencer marketing effectiveness, which is also in this catalog.

resources.title: Browsing the Aisles or Browsing the App? How Online Grocery Shopping is Changing What We Buy
resources.authors: Chintala, S. C.; Liaukonytė, J.; Yang, N.
resources.summary: Household panel evidence on how the same shoppers' baskets differ when they buy groceries online versus in store: fewer impulse and unhealthy items and more repetition online, with implications for new-product introduction.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor's own paper; a natural M2/M6 case. Pairs with the synthetic Instacart vs. in-person grocery data used in MBA 542 Module 1.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 1 reading list. The summary is high-level; check the wording against the published abstract before quoting it on the wiki.

resources.title: Mobile App Introduction and Online and Offline Purchases and Product Returns
resources.summary: Estimates how adopting a retailer's mobile app changes customers' online and offline purchases and product returns, using a quasi-experimental design that compares adopters with matched non-adopters.
resources.wiki_use: A marketing quasi-experiment by the course's previous instructor; useful continuity for students and a clean worked example of difference-in-differences with matching.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 1 reading list.

resources.title: Data Science for Business: What You Need to Know about Data Mining and Data-Analytic Thinking
resources.summary: Widely used business-school text on data-analytic thinking: framing problems as classification, regression or ranking; overfitting and holdout evaluation; expected-value framing of model decisions; churn and targeting examples.
resources.wiki_use: Conceptual companion to the hands-on ML material; its expected-value framework fits churn and targeting exercises.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 8 reading list. The O'Reilly link may need institutional access.

resources.title: Evaluating Recommendation Systems
resources.summary: Standard reference on offline, user-study and online evaluation of recommenders, covering accuracy plus coverage, novelty, diversity, serendipity and trust.
resources.wiki_use: Reference for an M7 exercise that moves beyond accuracy, such as diversity-aware re-ranking on the MBA 542 Netflix viewing data.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 5 reading list. Check that the Microsoft Research page links a PDF.

resources.title: Reducing Recommender System Biases: An Investigation of Rating Display Designs
resources.authors: Adomavicius, G.; Bockstedt, J. C.; Curley, S. P.; Zhang, J.
resources.summary: Experiments show that displayed recommendation ratings anchor consumers' own ratings, and test display designs that reduce the bias. Recommenders thereby shape the very data they are later trained on.
resources.wiki_use: Discussion reading on feedback loops between recommendation and measurement; ties M7 to M6.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 5 reading list. The MISQ URL contains a typo ('reeducing') on the publisher's own site.

resources.title: SMOTE: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique
resources.authors: Chawla, N. V.; Bowyer, K. W.; Hall, L. O.; Kegelmeyer, W. P.
resources.summary: Introduces oversampling of rare classes by interpolating synthetic minority examples, a standard tool for churn and response models where positives are rare.
resources.wiki_use: Background for an imbalanced-churn exercise. Also a good AI-coding check: oversampling before the train/test split leaks information, and AI-written pipelines often make that mistake.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 8 reading list. In practice, class weights or threshold tuning often work as well as SMOTE.

resources.title: The Power of Generative Marketing: Can Generative AI Create Superhuman Visual Marketing Content?
resources.authors: Hartmann, J.; Exner, Y.; Domdey, S.
resources.venue: International Journal of Research in Marketing 42(1), 13–31
resources.summary: Compares AI-generated with human-made marketing images at scale, finding that current generative models can match or exceed human-made visuals on quality and realism measures.
resources.wiki_use: Evidence for the M8 GenAI-in-marketing discussion. Check the study designs before using it as an M6 example.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 6 reading list. DOI not confirmed in a search result.

resources.title: Frontiers: Generative AI and Personalized Video Advertisements
resources.summary: Studies the effectiveness of generative-AI personalized video ads relative to non-personalized versions.
resources.wiki_use: Fills a gap the main search flagged (no good piece on GenAI personalization). Check its design and findings before pairing it with M6.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 6 reading list. The summary is deliberately brief because the paper itself was not opened; MIT IDE has a research brief (https://ide.mit.edu/insights/personalized-ai-video-ads).

resources.title: The Caring Machine: Feeling AI for Customer Care
resources.summary: Conceptual framework for using generative 'feeling AI' to deliver empathetic customer care and build customer lifetime value. The link is the AMA's summary of the article.
resources.wiki_use: Optional M8 reading if the course touches AI customer service.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 4 reading list. A corrigendum was published (https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/full/10.1177/00222429241270362). The article's own DOI was not confirmed.

resources.title: Scaling Trends for Data Poisoning in LLMs
resources.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 39
resources.summary: Shows that larger language models learn harmful behavior from small amounts of poisoned fine-tuning data more quickly than smaller ones, so scale does not protect against data poisoning.
resources.wiki_use: Background for an M8 discussion of poisoned online data (e.g., coordinated reviews or synthetic posts) feeding marketing models and AI assistants.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 8 reading list.

resources.title: Vulnerabilities in AI Code Generators: Exploring Targeted Data Poisoning Attacks
resources.authors: Cotroneo, D.; Improta, C.; Liguori, P.; Natella, R.
resources.venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Program Comprehension (ICPC 2024)
resources.summary: Shows that injecting a small share of poisoned training examples can make AI code generators emit vulnerable code for targeted prompts while overall accuracy stays normal, which makes the attack hard to detect.
resources.wiki_use: Supports the course rule that AI-written code is reviewed and tested, not trusted; pairs with the slopsquatting and code-security readings in this folder.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 8 reading list. The author list is from recollection of the arXiv entry; confirm it before citing. IEEE Xplore record: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10556436.

resources.title: Precision Retailing: Driving Results with Behavioral Insights and Data Analytics
resources.authors: Dubé, L.; Cohen, M.; Yang, N.; Monla, B. (eds.)
resources.summary: Edited volume on combining behavioral insight and data analytics in retail, co-edited by the instructor.
resources.wiki_use: Optional instructor-authored background; individual chapters could anchor M1 framing or M8 retail topics.
resources.notes: Also on the MBA 542 Module 1 reading list.

resources.section: Python for marketing analytics: notebooks and code
resources.subtopic: Marketing analytics textbook code (pandas 2, PyMC-Marketing, conjoint, CLV, MMM)
resources.title: Data Analytics for Marketing: A practical guide to analyzing marketing data using Python (companion code)
resources.summary: Notebooks for a 2024 Packt book: data extraction and EDA with pandas, Streamlit presentation (ch3), econometrics and causal inference with statsmodels/PyMC (ch4), forecasting, segmentation and RFM (ch7), CLV with PyMC-Marketing (ch8), survey analysis (ch9), conjoint with statsmodels (ch10), multi-touch attribution (ch11), MMM (ch12) and Bayesian experiments (ch13).
resources.wiki_use: Closest single match to the M1–M4 module spine; embed the ch7 RFM, ch8 CLV and ch10 conjoint notebooks as in-class coding activities.
resources.notes: No Chapter01 folder. Chapter11 (attribution) is left out because its 'attribution data markov chain.csv' is 44 MB; add it only if needed. The README pins PyMC-Marketing 0.3.1 and PyMC 5.11; PyMC-Marketing's CLV/MMM API has changed a lot since then, so expect to update the ch8 and ch12 calls (a good AI-assisted debugging exercise). The author also runs a paid 'MMM with Claude Code' workshop (see maven-mmm-with-claude-code).

resources.section: Python for marketing analytics: notebooks and code
resources.subtopic: Practitioner guide: causal inference, segmentation, CLV, elasticity, MMM
resources.title: Marketing Science in Python: A Practitioner's Guide (companion code)
resources.license: MIT (code and notebooks); book text all rights reserved
resources.summary: 14 recent notebooks: A/B tests, quasi-experiments, CausalImpact, meta-learners and uplift (Part 3); traditional and embedding-based segmentation plus CLV with PyMC-Marketing (Part 4); price elasticity, assortment optimization and forecasting (Part 5); Meridian MMM and geo experiments (Part 6). Includes small synthetic datasets and Colab badges.
resources.wiki_use: Use sec5.1_price_elasticity for M3, sec4.1 and sec4.2 (segmentation, CLV) for M4, and the Part 3 notebooks for M6. All are current-API examples worth embedding.
resources.notes: Public course mirror retains explicitly licensed Python and notebooks; other downloaded prose, data, figures, and configuration remain Dropbox-only. LICENSE-CODE explicitly covers notebooks. Do not copy the book manuscript, which lives elsewhere. Larger public datasets (Dunnhumby, Online Retail II, MineThatData) are not redistributed; data/raw/README.md explains how to get them. ai_angle refers to the embedding-based ('semantic') segmentation notebook. The author gave related PyData NYC 2023, PyData London 2024 and SciPy 2024 talks.

download.license: MIT (LICENSE-CODE, covering *.ipynb, *.py and src/msbook); prose under LICENSE is all rights reserved

resources.section: Python for marketing analytics: notebooks and code
resources.title: Marketing Analytics and Data Science: Tools and Models (supplementary code)
resources.summary: Chapter notebooks and CSVs from a 2026 textbook by a marketing professor: coding basics, data sources, MMM, segmentation (with a 2 MB customer-purchase dataset), two targeting chapters (bank marketing), forecasting, Bayes, Thompson sampling, causal inference, and an AI chapter with a Gemini example notebook. Several chapters include homework solution notebooks.
resources.wiki_use: Ready-made homework sets with solutions. The ch5 segmentation and ch4 MMM notebooks fit M4/M8, and the Gemini notebook is an AI-assisted example.
resources.notes: Small and new (4 stars, pushed 2026-02). Folder names contain spaces (e.g., 'Chapter 05 - Segmentation'). The book is likely available through SpringerLink at UIUC. Homework solutions are public, so don't reuse them verbatim as graded work.

resources.section: Python for marketing analytics: notebooks and code
resources.subtopic: Conjoint (traditional and CBC), clustering, MDS/perceptual maps, MNL, sample size
resources.title: pyrsm example notebooks (Rady School of Management business-analytics toolkit)
resources.summary: Example notebooks for the pyrsm package used in UCSD Rady's MSBA, with classic marketing datasets: traditional and choice-based conjoint (carpet, mp3, movie, minivan), hierarchical and k-means clustering, MDS and attribute perceptual maps (toothpaste, city, retailers), MNL on ketchup choice data, logistic/linear regression, uplift, experimental design and sample-size tools.
resources.wiki_use: Best open source of M4 conjoint and perceptual-map exercises in Python. Assign multivariate-conjoint and multivariate-cbc, and use design-sample-size in M6.
resources.notes: PyPI lists vnijs/pyrsm as the source, but its README links examples to radiant-ai-hub/pyrsm (pushed 2026-10-20, 4 stars), which is the repo verified here. The whole examples/ folder is 58 MB; the list above skips examples/data/model/fraud_data.parquet (13.5 MB) and the large ML regression notebooks. AGPL is OSI-approved, so mirroring is fine, but derived code must stay AGPL. The repo has a .claude/skills/pyrsm-regress skill link and a regress-skill-test notebook, an early AI-assisted workflow. The Rady pyrsm/Radiant entry in DATASETS_TEXTBOOKS.yaml covers the package; this entry is the notebook download.

resources.section: Python for marketing analytics: notebooks and code
resources.subtopic: Segmentation, regression for customer revenue, churn classification
resources.title: Data Science for Marketing Analytics, Second Edition (companion code)
resources.authors: Baig, M. R.; Govindan, G.; Shrimali, V. R.
resources.summary: Exercise and activity notebooks for 9 chapters: data preparation and cleaning, EDA and visualization, unsupervised segmentation and choosing a segmentation approach, predicting customer revenue with linear regression, evaluating regression models, churn prediction, tuning classifiers and multiclass classification.
resources.wiki_use: Step-by-step exercise format suits in-class coding for non-CS students. Ch3–4 (segmentation) map to M4 and ch5–6 to M3.

The code dates from 2021 (pandas 1.x and older scikit-learn), so expect small API fixes. PacktPublishing/Data-Science-for-Marketing-Analytics and the '...Workshop' repo both redirect here.

resources.notes: Archived 2026-04-18 (read-only). The data-prep notebook downloads a 21 GB Kaggle file, which the download machine can't reach. The README says results are cached, but plan to substitute a smaller dataset.

resources.notes: Size unverified (tree API failed). Most exercises load data from raw GitHub URLs, which works from Colab. Some solutions use pre-pandas-2 idioms.

Its notebooks/events_analysis.ipynb (6 MB) holds saved widget state with real-looking GA4 event values, including a Log4j-style JNDI probe string captured from traffic; it's harmless in Python but should be cleared before reuse. resources.wiki_use: Main in-class lab for incrementality: design a single-cell holdback test, then analyze it and talk about how the lift result would calibrate an MMM.
resources.notes: Last commit 2026-10-01, actively developed. pip install meridian-geox. Needs Python 3.10 or later, or 3.11 or later alongside Meridian. This is the natural successor to trimmed_match and matched_markets for teaching, and pairs with google/meridian, which is already in the library.

resources.summary: Python library with a C++ core for robust iROAS estimation in matched-pair geo experiments. Includes Colab notebooks for design (with cross-validation) and post-analysis, plus example datasets.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor background or an optional deep dive on matched-pair geo designs and outlier-robust iROAS. The README's five-pair iROAS example makes a good worked illustration.
resources.notes: Last commit 2023-06-01. Not archived, but dormant. Installing it builds a C++ extension with bazel, which is slow and fragile on current Colab. The README says it was tested on Python 3.7. Prefer Meridian GeoX for student labs.

resources.wiki_use: Compact TBR example to set beside Meridian GeoX or Orduz's PyMC TBR notebook, so students can see one method in three implementations.
resources.notes: Last commit 2025-08-21. The README says 'not an officially supported Google product; for research purposes only'.

resources.section: Python for marketing analytics: notebooks and code

Uses a crossover design, CUPED adjustment for pre-period performance, and outlier trimming. It is the recommended test method for FeedGen, Google's LLM feed optimizer.
resources.wiki_use: Strong bridge case for M6 and M8: students design and analyze an experiment that tests whether LLM-rewritten product titles actually lift clicks, so they practice CUPED and power analysis on a real marketing decision.
resources.notes: Last commit 2026-10-21, very active. Needs Python 3.10 or later. The sister repo google-marketing-solutions/feedgen (LLM feed rewriting) is Apps Script/TypeScript with no notebooks, so link to it rather than download it.

resources.summary: Python package from Spotify's experimentation team for frequentist and Bayesian A/B test analysis, sample-size calculation, group sequential testing and regression-based variance reduction. Example notebooks are in examples/.
resources.wiki_use: In-class demo of 'peeking' and why sequential boundaries matter. Use the Sequential and Sample-sizing notebooks as worked examples.
resources.notes: Last commit 2026-02-26. Latest release badge shows 4.1.0. The notebooks are mostly code with little explanatory text, so pair them with the Courthoud or Trencseni write-ups. The Bayesian and Frequentist example notebooks (7.4 MB) are left out to save space.

resources.section: Python for marketing analytics: notebooks and code
resources.title: Bayesian CUPED (NumPyro tutorial)
resources.authors: NumPyro contributors (adapted from Orduz, J. and Courthoud, M.)

resources.wiki_use: A sharp caution for interpreting recommender A/B tests in M6: winning an experiment and serving users are not the same thing.
resources.verified_via: local full-text sections and/or primary publication, 2026-10-23
resources.notes: Seven-author list and December 2023 version checked against supplied PDF and arXiv. Local filename contains 2022, the first arXiv submission year. Benchmark experiments are not a general field estimate of manipulation.

resources.title: Unintended Consequences of Recommender System Interventions: Evidence from a Field Experiment
resources.authors: Luo, S.; Yao, S.; Zhang, D. J.
resources.summary: Studies a temporary ranking boost for celebrity sleep-reminder videos in a randomized platform campaign. The analyzed active-user panel shows increased late-night and overall usage, with persistence after the campaign. The authors relate persistence to training signals and policy updates generated by the intervention.
resources.wiki_use: Recent example for the M6/M7 discussion of spillovers and unintended outcomes in platform experiments.
resources.verified_via: local full-text sections and/or primary publication, 2026-10-23
resources.notes: Local Sections 4.2–4.3 and Table 6 checked. The analyzed panel contains 200,000 users active on the first experiment day. Reported 14.75% and 2.18% figures are relative assignment effects on usage. Mechanism attribution and sample inclusion require separate attention.

resources.title: Is Seeing Believing? How Recommender Interfaces Affect Users' Opinions
resources.authors: Cosley, D.; Lam, S. K.; Albert, I.; Konstan, J. A.; Riedl, J.
resources.summary: Classic experiment in which showing users (sometimes manipulated) predicted ratings pulls their own re-ratings toward the displayed value: recommender interfaces anchor opinions.
resources.wiki_use: Short classic that pairs with Adomavicius et al. (2019) in this folder; useful for discussing how recommenders contaminate the ratings they learn from.

resources.title: Steering via Algorithmic Recommendations
resources.summary: Empirical study of Amazon self-preferencing using product recommendation records and within-product variation from Amazon stockouts. Seller identity affects receipt of Frequently Bought Together recommendations, with controls and falsification checks addressing alternative explanations.
resources.wiki_use: Case on platform incentives and observational identification in M6/M8. Explain the stockout comparison, accompanying price and availability changes, and the distinction between platform return and customer value.
resources.verified_via: local full-text sections and/or primary publication, 2026-10-23
resources.notes: Corrected the earlier theory-only description. Publisher metadata verifies the 2024 article; the supplied local working paper is dated December 2020 despite 2021 in its filename.

resources.title: Beyond Persuasion: Towards Conversational Recommender System with Credible Explanations
resources.authors: Qin, P.; Huang, C.; Deng, Y.; Lei, W.; Chua, T.-S.
resources.summary: Shows that LLM-based conversational recommenders can persuade users with explanations that are not credible, and proposes a method that keeps explanations persuasive but grounded in true item facts.
resources.wiki_use: Counterpoint to RecPIE: LLM explanations can improve recommendations, but they can also mislead. Good for a class debate on AI shopping assistants (M8).
resources.verified_via: local full-text sections and/or primary publication, 2026-10-23
resources.notes: Authors, venue, and pages verified against ACL Anthology and supplied PDF. PC-CRS evaluates credibility and persuasion separately; M7 connects the distinction to attribute-level factual checks.

resources.title: GitHub Pages limits
resources.summary: Official GitHub Pages limits: a published site can be at most 1 GB, and the source repo should stay under 1 GB. Soft limits are 100 GB/month of bandwidth and 10 builds/hour (custom GitHub Actions builds are exempt), and deployments time out after 10 minutes. Pages is not meant for commercial or sensitive-transaction sites.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only planning: keep the wiki's datasets and media under these caps, host large data elsewhere (GitHub Releases, Box, Hugging Face), and never collect passwords or student data on the site.
resources.notes: Rate-limited requests get HTTP 429. Custom domains use a CNAME record for a subdomain or A/ALIAS/ANAME for an apex domain; verify the domain first to prevent takeover (https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/about-custom-domains-and-github-pages, fetched). A campus subdomain such as *.illinois.edu would need campus DNS cooperation; that is my inference, not from GitHub's docs.

resources.title: Using custom workflows with GitHub Pages
resources.summary: How to build and deploy a Pages site with GitHub Actions using actions/configure-pages@v5, actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4 and actions/deploy-pages@v4 (the examples also use actions/checkout@v6). The deploy job needs the pages: write and id-token: write permissions.
resources.wiki_use: Reference for the wiki's build pipeline; Quarto, Jupyter Book 2, marimo and JupyterLite sites all deploy this way.
resources.notes: The artifact must be a gzipped tar under 10 GB with no symbolic or hard links. Action versions are as shown on 2026-10-23; pin them in the workflow file.

resources.title: GitHub Classroom deprecated
resources.summary: GitHub Classroom shut down on 2026-08-28, including its website, APIs and services. Classroom and assignment names, tests defined outside repos and LTI rosters will be deleted; user accounts, repos and organizations stay.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only: don't build the course's assignment distribution on GitHub Classroom. Use Classroom 50, Codio, or plain template repositories instead.
resources.notes: New sign-ups ended 2026-05-26 (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-26-github-classroom-sign-ups-are-no-longer-available, fetched). GitHub's migration page names Codio and Classroom 50 as partner options and describes a gh CLI export utility (https://docs.github.com/en/education/manage-coursework-with-github-classroom/get-started-with-github-classroom/export-or-migrate-github-classroom-data, fetched). Older GitHub Education pages still describe Classroom as active and are stale.

resources.title: Classroom 50
resources.authors: Classroom 50 (reported to be the Fifty Foundation, the nonprofit behind CS50)
resources.summary: Free, open-source replacement for GitHub Classroom that distributes and autogrades programming assignments in GitHub repos. Features include template repos, due dates, individual or group work, pytest or input/output tests, CSV rosters and score export.
resources.wiki_use: Candidate tool for handing out starter notebooks and programming assignments through GitHub, linked from the wiki's assignment pages.
resources.notes: The sponsoring organization and the feature list come from a third-party blog (https://bruceelgort.com/2026/07/20/github-classroom-is-gone-heres-the-free-tool-that-replaces-it/, fetched); the official homepage only says it is the free, open-source alternative to GitHub Classroom, with no license named. It needs a GitHub organization on a Team plan (free for verified educators) and broad read/write access to the org's repos. It reached general availability on 2026-07-01 per GitHub's migration doc. It is new, so pilot it before relying on it. The repo (foundation50/classroom50, GPL-3.0) says it is supported by the Fifty Foundation; only a third-party blog says that foundation is the nonprofit behind CS50.

resources.title: About GitHub Education for teachers
resources.summary: Benefits for verified faculty at accredited institutions: a free GitHub Team plan (unlimited users and private repos) and a free GitHub Copilot Pro subscription.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only: create a course GitHub organization for the wiki repo and team projects, and use Copilot Pro to demonstrate AI-assisted coding in class.
resources.notes: Copilot Pro setup for teachers: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/set-up-copilot/enable-copilot/set-up-for-teachers-and-os-maintainers (seen in search, not fetched). This page still refers to GitHub Classroom as active, which is stale after the August 2026 shutdown. Student benefits were not checked here; check the campus program first.

resources.title: Netlify pricing update: introducing credit-based plans
resources.summary: Since 2025-09-05, Netlify plans run on credits. The free plan gives 300 credits a month. Each production deploy costs 15 credits, bandwidth 10 credits per GB, and web requests 3 credits per 10,000; preview deploys are free.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only comparison: at 15 credits per production deploy, a free Netlify site allows at most about 20 deploys a month even before bandwidth. That is tight for a wiki updated often; GitHub Pages has no such meter.
resources.notes: Cloudflare Pages' free plan allows 500 builds a month, 20,000 files per site and 25 MiB per file (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/platform/limits, fetched). Both hosts offer deploy previews, which GitHub Pages lacks. Netlify's changelog does not say what happens when free credits run out.

resources.title: Quarto
resources.summary: Open-source, Pandoc-based publishing system that turns .qmd, .ipynb and Markdown files containing Python or R code into websites, books, slides and PDFs. Websites get navigation, cross-references and a built-in local search index.
resources.wiki_use: Leading candidate engine for the Marketing Analytics wiki. One source produces pages, slides and notebooks, and freeze means heavy Python runs only on the instructor's machine.
resources.notes: Version status on 2026-10-23: 1.10.x is the current stable line (GitHub marks v1.10.18 as Latest, July 2026), and 1.11.x is in pre-release. Quarto 1.9 (2026-03-24, https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2026-03-24_1.9-release/, fetched) added 'llms-txt: true' for websites, which writes an llms.txt index plus a .llms.md copy of each page so students can feed the wiki to an AI assistant. It also made opt-in (express) cookie consent the default, added screen-reader labels for videos, and added experimental PDF/UA output. Release posts now live on opensource.posit.co. Algolia is an optional alternative to the built-in search.

resources.title: Quarto: GitHub Pages publishing guide
resources.summary: Covers three ways to publish: render to a docs/ folder, run 'quarto publish gh-pages', or use a GitHub Action (quarto-dev/quarto-actions/publish@v2). Also explains 'execute: freeze: auto', which runs code locally and commits the results in _freeze.
resources.wiki_use: Step-by-step deployment for a Quarto wiki. Freeze avoids rebuilding Python environments in CI on every commit.
resources.notes: Add a .nojekyll file when publishing from docs/. The Action route needs read/write workflow permissions.

resources.title: Quarto Live: interactive code blocks and exercises (webR and Pyodide)
resources.summary: Quarto extension that adds editable, runnable R (webR) and Python (Pyodide) code blocks to HTML pages. It supports exercises with blanks, hints, solutions and custom grading, all running in the browser on any static host such as GitHub Pages.
resources.wiki_use: Embed in-browser Python practice cells and auto-checked exercises in wiki pages so students can try code without Colab or a local install.
resources.notes: The 0.1.1 announcement (https://tidyverse.org/blog/2024/10/quarto-live-0-1-1/, fetched) explains exercise, setup and check blocks. The repo (https://github.com/r-wasm/quarto-live, MIT) has no tagged releases and shows a 0.1.2-dev version. The docs site was rebuilt with Quarto 1.9.38 in 2026, but recent commit dates could not be confirmed, so treat it as early-stage (0.x). The community alternative coatless-quarto/pyodide (https://github.com/coatless-quarto/pyodide) itself points users to quarto-live as the official option.

resources.title: Quarto extensions listing: filters
resources.summary: Official directory of Quarto filter extensions. Quiz and exercise options include quizdown, shortiquiz, stepbystep (guided tasks with progress checkboxes) and assign (instructions paired with solutions).
resources.wiki_use: Shortlist of self-check and exercise widgets to embed in module pages.
resources.notes: Repos named in the listing: https://github.com/parmsam/quarto-quizdown, https://github.com/skyfroger/stepbystep and https://github.com/coatless-quarto/assign. I did not fetch these individually; check license and activity before adopting.

resources.title: shortiquiz: interactive quiz questions for Quarto HTML documents
resources.summary: Quarto extension offering multiple-choice, multi-answer, text-input, dropdown, Parsons (reorder lines of code), image-hotspot, flashcard and gated-stage questions. Install with 'quarto add skyfroger/shortiquiz'.
resources.wiki_use: Low-stakes self-checks at the end of each module page. Parsons problems suit code-reading practice for non-CS students checking AI-generated code.
resources.notes: GPL-3.0 copyleft applies to the extension code shipped with the site. The repo has 59 commits; the last-commit date was not visible. Answers sit in the page source, so use it for ungraded practice only and keep graded quizzes in Canvas.

resources.title: Jupyter Book 2
resources.summary: Jupyter Book 2 was released the week of 2025-11-04, keeping the jupyter-book package name, and is rebuilt on the MyST Document Engine. Authors write in notebooks or MyST Markdown and get cross-references, build-time execution, and interactivity in the browser or through Binder/JupyterHub.
resources.wiki_use: Strong alternative to Quarto if the wiki is notebook-first; it is the stack behind the Data 8 textbook and QuantEcon-style lecture sites.
resources.notes: Known limitations versus v1 (https://jupyterbook.org/stable/resources/faq, fetched): pretty URLs, so my_page.html becomes /my-page/; myst.yml replaces _config.yml; not yet at parity on execution features, editable Thebe cells or autodoc. The v1 Sphinx stack is 'mostly in maintenance mode'; pin jupyter-book<2 to stay on v1. Release rationale: https://jupyterbook.org/blog/posts/2025-11-04-why-make-a-major-release. The blog shows active 2026 development: mystmd 1.8.2 (Mar 2026), an AnyWidget directive (Mar 2026), accessibility work on the MyST theme (May 2026), a 'Demystifying MyST Markdown in Education' event (Apr 2026) and a new release (Sep 2026).

resources.title: MyST guide: exercises and solutions
resources.summary: Documents MyST's numbered {exercise} directive and linked {solution} directive, including hidden and dropdown options. Gated start/end syntax lets executable code cells sit inside exercises while staying notebook-compatible.
resources.wiki_use: Pattern for in-text exercises with collapsible solutions if the wiki is built with Jupyter Book 2 / MyST.
resources.notes: There is no built-in quiz or auto-grading; pair with JupyterLite or Pyodide cells for runnable code.

resources.title: Material for MkDocs Insiders – now free for everyone
resources.summary: Announces that Material for MkDocs 9.7.0 is the final feature release. The project is in maintenance mode with no new features, Insiders features are now free, and development moves to Zensical.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only: the reason not to start a new course wiki on MkDocs + Material in 2026.
resources.notes: Follow-up post on 2026-02-18 (https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/, fetched): MkDocs 1.x is unmaintained. MkDocs 2.0 is a pre-release rewrite with TOML config and no plugin system, and Material will not support it. Material 9.7.5 pins MkDocs <2.0, and critical maintenance is extended through 2027-05-05. Material's GitHub Discussions went read-only in November 2025.

resources.title: Zensical
resources.summary: Successor static site generator from the makers of Material for MkDocs. It reads existing mkdocs.yml projects and adds faster differential rebuilds and a new client-side search engine (Disco).
resources.wiki_use: Keep on the watch list if a Markdown-only docs look is preferred; it is too young to be the main engine for an upcoming semester.
resources.notes: Status on 2026-10-23: pre-0.1 (the site is built with zensical 0.0.70). A 'dependable release line' starting with 0.1 is scheduled for 2026-11-05. Only a subset of MkDocs plugins is supported. An October 2026 update says the planned Rust Markdown parser has been replaced by a Python-Markdown-compatible one. Announcement: https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2025/11/05/zensical/. It has no notebook-execution story comparable to Quarto or MyST.

resources.title: Docusaurus blog and releases
resources.summary: React/MDX documentation-site generator from Meta. Version 3.10 (2026-04-07) is announced as the last release in the v3 line, ahead of v4.
resources.wiki_use: Optional, and only if the wiki needs custom React components. Its JavaScript toolchain is heavier than Quarto or MyST for a non-CS course.
resources.notes: Docusaurus has no native notebook execution, so Python content must be pre-rendered. A v4 major release is coming; expect migration work.

resources.title: Starlight (Astro documentation framework)
resources.summary: Astro-based docs framework with built-in navigation, i18n, dark mode, Markdown/MDX/Markdoc, and Pagefind search that needs no configuration.
resources.wiki_use: Optional fast, accessible site shell if the wiki is mostly prose plus embedded HTML artifacts.
resources.notes: Still pre-1.0 (v0.42.6 per site metadata). Pagefind is the default search; Algolia DocSearch is available through a plugin (https://starlight.astro.build/guides/site-search/, fetched). Repo: https://github.com/withastro/starlight (MIT).

resources.title: VitePress
resources.summary: Vite + Vue static site generator for Markdown documentation. The site lists 2.0.0-alpha.20 as current and keeps docs for the 1.6.4 stable line.
resources.wiki_use: Optional; similar trade-offs to Docusaurus, with Vue components instead of React.
resources.notes: 2.0 was still in alpha on 2026-10-23. Repo: https://github.com/vuejs/vitepress.

resources.title: Pyodide changelog
resources.summary: Pyodide, CPython compiled to WebAssembly, is the engine under quarto-live, JupyterLite, marimo WASM and PyScript. The 314.x line (314.0.0 on 2026-06-09) runs Python 3.14, and 314.0.7 (2026-09-14) is the latest release.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only reference for which Python version and package builds students get in any in-browser cell.
resources.notes: Version numbers jumped from 0.x (0.28 shipped Python 3.13) to 314.x. The changelog announces no policy, so the link to the Python version is my inference. 0.29.5 and 0.27.8 got Node 26 fixes in September 2026. Pure-Python wheels install through micropip.

resources.title: Packages built in Pyodide
resources.summary: List of compiled packages shipped with Pyodide 314.0.7, including pandas 3.0.2, scikit-learn 1.8.0, statsmodels 0.14.6, scipy 1.18.0, matplotlib 3.10.8 and numpy 2.4.6. Seaborn is not on the built-in list.
resources.wiki_use: Check before writing in-browser exercises: the core M2–M7 stack (pandas wrangling, statsmodels OLS/logit, scikit-learn clustering and prediction) runs in the browser.
resources.notes: Trade-offs: the first page load downloads the runtime and packages. marimo's docs cite a 2 GB memory cap and no true threading or multiprocessing under WASM. Packages with compiled code that are not on this list (for example PyTorch) generally won't install. Seaborn is pure Python and should install through micropip (not tested). pandas 3.0 is a major release, so syntax can differ from older tutorials and from whatever pandas version Colab ships; check version parity before mixing Colab and in-browser cells.

resources.title: JupyterLite documentation
resources.summary: A JupyterLab and Notebook distribution that runs entirely in the browser, with Pyodide or Xeus Python kernels in Web Workers. It deploys as a static site with no server.
resources.wiki_use: Give students a full notebook interface from a wiki link (for example a 'Try it' button on each module) with no accounts or installs.
resources.notes: The docs were labeled 0.8.6 when fetched, while their compatibility table listed jupyterlite-core 0.7.0 (bundling JupyterLab 4.5 and Notebook 7.5); confirm the current version before pinning. Only the last two releases are supported. Not every JupyterLab feature works. Student files are kept in browser storage, so test how work persists before relying on it for assignments.

resources.title: jupyterlite/demo: template for deploying JupyterLite to GitHub Pages
resources.summary: Template repo that builds a JupyterLite site and deploys it to GitHub Pages with GitHub Actions. Notebooks go in the content folder, and kernels and extensions are listed in requirements.txt.
resources.wiki_use: Use as the template for a Marketing Analytics 'lab' subsite that holds the module notebooks and is linked from the wiki.
resources.notes: Deploy guide (https://jupyterlite.readthedocs.io/en/stable/quickstart/deploy.html, fetched): click 'Use this template', enable Actions, set workflow permissions to read/write and the Pages source to GitHub Actions. For pre-installed packages, use the xeus-python demo with an environment.yml. Live demo at jupyterlite.github.io/demo. Requires Firefox 90+ or Chromium 89+.

resources.title: marimo WebAssembly notebooks
resources.summary: marimo's reactive notebooks can run entirely in the browser through Pyodide. numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas and matplotlib are pre-installed, and other pure-Python wheels install automatically on import.
resources.wiki_use: Build reactive demos (for example sliders driving a CLV or conjoint simulator), export them as static HTML, and embed them in wiki pages.
resources.notes: Export with 'marimo export html-wasm notebook.py -o out --mode run' for a read-only app or '--mode edit' for an editable notebook. The export must be served over HTTP, not opened from file://, and Pyodide and packages load from a CDN. Run 'marimo check --select MW' to catch incompatible packages (https://docs.marimo.io/guides/exporting/webassembly_html/, fetched). Limits: 2 GB memory, emulated concurrency, no PDB. marimo islands, which embed single reactive cells in any HTML page, are still a 'Preview' feature (https://docs.marimo.io/guides/island_example/, fetched).

resources.title: marimo: reactive Python notebook (GitHub repository)
resources.summary: Open-source reactive Python notebook stored as plain .py files. It has a built-in AI assistant that sees in-memory variables, Copilot completion, bring-your-own-key or local models, and 'marimo pair' for working alongside Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode.
resources.wiki_use: Option for in-class vibe-coding activities: notebooks diff cleanly in Git and work with coding agents, and the same files export to WASM pages for the wiki.
resources.notes: 22.3k stars when fetched. The latest release number was not visible on the fetched page.

resources.title: PyScript
resources.summary: Open-source platform for running Python inside web pages. The current release is 2026.7.3 (year-based version numbers), with docs at pyscript.github.io/docs/latest/.
resources.wiki_use: Optional for hand-built plain-HTML widgets; for course notebooks, quarto-live, JupyterLite or marimo are more turnkey.
resources.notes: The fetched homepage names neither its runtimes nor its license; check the docs before adopting.

resources.title: Binder (mybinder.org) user guidelines
resources.summary: Free service that launches a GitHub repo of notebooks in a temporary cloud Jupyter session. Sessions get 1–2 GB of RAM, shut down after 10 minutes idle, last up to about 6 hours, and are capped at 100 simultaneous users per repository.
resources.wiki_use: Fallback 'Launch Binder' button for notebooks that need packages Pyodide lacks. The 100-user cap and slow cold starts make it unreliable for a whole class at once.
resources.notes: The mybinder.org homepage says the service is 'currently in testing'. Thebe (https://github.com/jupyter-book/thebe, BSD-3-Clause, fetched) turns static code cells into runnable ones backed by a Jupyter server, or by JupyterLite through thebe-lite. Thebe 0.9.0 is still in development, and Jupyter Book 2 does not yet support editable Thebe cells.

resources.title: Using Google Colab with GitHub (colab-github-demo notebook)
resources.summary: Official Colab notebook explaining the colab.research.google.com/github/<org>/<repo>/blob/<branch>/<path>.ipynb URL pattern and the 'Open In Colab' badge in Markdown and HTML. It also covers saving copies to Drive or back to GitHub, and access to private repos.
resources.wiki_use: Put an Open in Colab badge on every wiki notebook so students can run the full analysis (with Gemini in Colab) on Google's servers.
resources.notes: Colab opens an editable copy and leaves the repo unchanged. Saving back to GitHub requires granting Colab permission to push commits. The notebook text was read from the raw.githubusercontent.com copy.

resources.title: H5P
resources.summary: Open HTML5 framework (MIT) for interactive content such as interactive video, presentations and quiz-style games. The paid H5P.com service adds LTI integration with Canvas and other LMSs.
resources.wiki_use: Optional for richer self-checks. On a static site, h5p-standalone (https://github.com/tunapanda/h5p-standalone, MIT, 3.x) plays .h5p packages without a server.
resources.notes: Authoring needs an H5P-enabled platform or H5P.com. The paid Premium tier adds AI-powered 'Smart Import'. Content embedded in a GitHub Pages wiki sends no grades back, so keep graded quizzes in Canvas.

resources.title: MLU-Explain
resources.summary: Interactive scrollytelling explainers covering linear and logistic regression, train/test/validation splits, cross-validation, precision and recall, ROC/AUC, decision trees, random forests, the bias-variance trade-off and double descent.
resources.wiki_use: Link or assign from the M3 and M7 pages; also a model for the visual-explainer style the wiki could adopt.
resources.notes: The GitHub repo was archived (read-only) on 2026-03-06, so expect no more updates; the site still loads. The site lists 14 articles and the repo holds 10.

resources.title: Seeing Theory
resources.authors: Kunin, D.; Guo, J.; Devlin, T. D.; Xiang, D.
resources.summary: Brown University's D3-based visual introduction to probability and statistics. It runs from basic probability through distributions, frequentist and Bayesian inference, and regression.
resources.wiki_use: Refresher links on the M3 (regression) and M6 (inference) pages for students who are rusty on statistics.
resources.notes: The site is now archived for reference. The page states no license. Source: https://github.com/seeingtheory/Seeing-Theory (license not checked).

resources.title: Distill Hiatus
resources.summary: Distill, the interactive machine-learning journal, paused publication in July 2021. Its archive of interactive articles and its article template remain models for explorable explanations.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only design inspiration for interactive figures; selected articles could be optional M7 reading.
resources.notes: The hiatus is open-ended, so expect no new articles. The Explorable Explanations hub (https://explorabl.es/, fetched) is a related source of interactive examples, though its subject listings did not render in the fetch.

resources.title: The Pudding
resources.summary: Digital publication of visual essays that explain ideas with data; still active, with new stories through October 2026.
resources.wiki_use: Examples of data storytelling for the M2 Pyramid Principle and visualization module, and models for the team blog-post deliverable.
resources.notes: Whether the stories' code is open source was not verified.

resources.title: Observable Framework
resources.summary: Open-source static site generator for data apps, dashboards and reports. Pages are Markdown with reactive JavaScript, and data loaders written in Python, R or SQL snapshot the data at build time.
resources.wiki_use: Option for interactive dashboards inside the wiki (for example a customer-segmentation explorer) where Python prepares the data at build time.
resources.notes: v1.13.4 per the site. The docs now live at observablehq.github.io/framework, and observablehq.com/framework redirects there. No maintenance notice was seen, but check recent activity before committing. Repo: https://github.com/observablehq/framework (ISC).

resources.title: Pagefind
resources.summary: Static search library that indexes the built HTML from any site generator and serves a chunked index. It claims a total payload under 300 kB for a full-text search of a 10,000-page site. The current version is 1.5.2.
resources.wiki_use: Adds search to a plain-HTML or mixed-tool wiki; it is also Starlight's default search.
resources.notes: Repo: https://github.com/pagefind/pagefind (MIT). Lunr.js (https://github.com/olivernn/lunr.js, MIT, fetched) is the older in-browser alternative; it shows 105 open issues and recent activity could not be confirmed. Quarto and Jupyter Book 2 have built-in search, so Pagefind matters mainly for plain-HTML builds.

resources.title: WCAG 2 Overview
resources.summary: W3C overview of WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 and the A, AA and AAA conformance levels. W3C recommends WCAG 2.2, which is backward compatible with 2.1 and is also published as ISO/IEC 40500:2025.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only reference for setting the wiki's accessibility target.
resources.notes: WCAG 2.1 was last updated 2025-05-06, and WCAG 3 is still an early draft. UIUC's own standard requires 2.2 AA for internally built web content (see uiuc-minimum-digital-accessibility-standards).

resources.title: WebAIM's WCAG 2 Checklist
resources.summary: Plain-language checklist of the WCAG 2.2 success criteria at levels A, AA and AAA, with filters for 2.0 and 2.1.
resources.wiki_use: QA checklist to run before each module page goes live: alt text, captions, 4.5:1 contrast, keyboard access, real headings, a lang attribute, and reflow at 200% zoom.
resources.notes: Last updated 2024-06-20. Interactive widgets (quizzes, sliders, in-browser code editors) need separate keyboard and screen-reader testing.

resources.title: ADA.gov fact sheet: Title II rule on web content and mobile app accessibility
resources.authors: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
resources.summary: The DOJ's ADA Title II rule requires web content from state and local governments, including public universities, to meet WCAG 2.1 AA. An April 2026 interim final rule moved compliance to 2027-04-26 for entities serving 50,000+ people and 2028-04-26 for smaller ones.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only: a public-university course wiki should meet WCAG 2.1 AA by April 2027 at the latest.
resources.notes: The exceptions for archived content and individualized password-protected documents are narrow and don't cover public HTML course pages. This is a summary, not legal advice. The page title shown here is paraphrased.

resources.title: University of Illinois Minimum Digital Accessibility Standards
resources.summary: Campus standard under the Digital Accessibility Policy (HR-86). Internally developed web content must meet the most recent recommended WCAG, currently 2.2 AA, use WAI-ARIA 1.2, and work with major browsers and screen readers. Course content and training materials are explicitly in scope.
resources.wiki_use: The binding target for the Marketing Analytics wiki: design to WCAG 2.2 AA and test with NVDA and VoiceOver.
resources.notes: Commercial SaaS is held to 2.1 AA. Campus resources: instructor tips at https://itaccessibility.illinois.edu/tips-instructor and evaluation tools at https://itaccessibility.illinois.edu/web-evaluation-tools (links seen on itaccessibility.illinois.edu). The page lists no deadlines.

resources.title: Intermediate Quantitative Economics with Python
resources.summary: QuantEcon's open course of 149 lectures, built with Jupyter Book and a QuantEcon theme. A 'Launch Notebook' button opens each lecture in Colab.
resources.wiki_use: Model for lecture-as-webpage design with downloadable notebooks and one-click Colab launch.
resources.notes: Source is MyST Markdown (repo lecture-python.myst), and the Colab links point to a generated lecture-python.notebooks repo. Whether it has moved to Jupyter Book 2 was not confirmed.

resources.title: UBC Master of Data Science: public course materials
resources.summary: Index of 25 UBC MDS courses (DSCI 511–591) linking to course repos: syllabi for all 25, lecture notes for 15 and labs for 7.
resources.wiki_use: Mine the syllabi, lab structure and rubrics when designing programming assignments; also a model for an open course repo.
resources.notes: Related UBC exemplars: 'Data Science: A First Introduction with Python' (https://python.datasciencebook.ca/, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, a Sphinx/Docutils site, probably Jupyter Book v1) and 'Programming in Python for Data Science' (https://prog-learn.mds.ubc.ca/, built on Ines Montani's Gatsby course-starter-python template, an older stack). The program site ubc-mds.github.io is built with Hugo.

resources.title: Teaching and Learning with Jupyter
resources.authors: Barba, L. A.; Barker, L. J.; Blank, D. S.; Brown, J.; Downey, A. B.; George, T.; Heagy, L. J.; Mandli, K. T.; Moore, J. K.; Lippert, D.; Niemeyer, K. E.; Watkins, R. R.; West, R. H.; Wickes, E.; Willing, C.; Zingale, M.
resources.summary: Open handbook on teaching with Jupyter. It includes a catalogue of 23 pedagogical patterns (for example 'Shift-Enter for the win', 'Fill in the blanks' and test-driven development) and practical chapters on running a class.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only guide for structuring in-class coding activities and notebook exercises on the wiki.
resources.notes: Built with bookdown/GitBook rather than Jupyter Book. Written in 2019, before AI coding assistants.

resources.title: Illinois Chat (formerly UIUC.chat) documentation
resources.authors: University of Illinois (Center for AI Innovation GitHub organization)
resources.summary: Campus-supported platform for building course chatbots over uploaded materials (PDFs, slides, videos, a web crawl, or a Canvas connection). Answers cite their sources, and a tutor-mode prompt is available. The official instance is chat.illinois.edu.
resources.wiki_use: Build a Marketing Analytics assistant grounded in the wiki by crawling the GitHub Pages site, and link it from every page.
resources.notes: UIUC.chat is moving to chat.illinois.edu, and chatbot creation is disabled on the old site (https://docs.uiuc.chat/migration/migrate-to-illinois-chat.md, fetched). Per the FAQ it is free to use but you supply your own OpenAI API key, and data is stored on AWS with no guarantees; the FAQ may predate the campus migration. Privacy: there is no FERPA statement and no documented iframe embed, so keep student records and grades out of it. Backend: https://github.com/Center-for-AI-Innovation/ai-ta-backend (public, MIT); access to the frontend repo appears restricted. Support: genaisupport@mx.uillinois.edu.

resources.title: CS50.ai (CS50 Duck)
resources.summary: CS50's ChatGPT-based 'duck debugger' for students and teachers, supported by Microsoft and OpenAI. It is the best-known example of a course-specific AI tutor.
resources.wiki_use: Instructor-only model for an AI-help policy and tutor design (guide students rather than solve for them).
resources.notes: The fetched page describes neither its guardrails nor whether courses outside CS50 can use it. A CS50 team paper at SIGCSE 2024 describes the design, but I did not verify its URL.
